title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 25
summary: It is Day 25 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: THOUSAND OAKS, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27, 1978: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Roger Staubach #12 practices at training camp at California Lutheran College on July 27, 1978 in Thousand Oaks, California. Staubach played his entire career with the Cowboys, from 1969-1979, where the six-time Pro Bowler and Heisman Trophy-winner led the offense to two Super Bowl championships. (Photo by James Drake/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 25 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. This is a big one for Day 25 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. Today we revisit the afternoon the Roger Staubach era officially began. Nearly five years after Dallas selected him in the tenth round of the 1964 NFL Draft, Staubach finally made his professional debut and immediately demonstrated the playmaking ability that would eventually transform the franchise. Sunday, September 21, 1969 Cotton Bowl, Dallas, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 24, St. Louis Cardinals 3 Staubach’s arrival had been delayed by his service commitment to the United States Navy, which included a tour in Vietnam. He joined a Cowboys team transitioning away from Don Meredith, with Craig Morton expected to remain the established starter. Tom Landry used both quarterbacks during the 1969 opener, but it was Staubach who produced the game’s defining moments. Dallas struck first when Staubach connected with Lance Rentzel for a 75-yard touchdown. It was the first touchdown pass of Staubach’s NFL career, giving the Cotton Bowl crowd an immediate glimpse of what the former Heisman Trophy winner could provide. St. Louis answered only with Jim Bakken’s 20-yard field goal, leaving Dallas ahead 7-3 at halftime. The Cowboys extended their lead through some Landry creativity in the third quarter. Rookie running back Calvin Hill took a handoff and threw a 53-yard touchdown pass to Rentzel, who had now scored on receptions from two different passers. Mike Clark’s extra point made it 14-3. Clark added a 30-yard field goal in the fourth quarter before Staubach completed the scoring himself. The rookie quarterback scrambled into the end zone from three yards out, giving him both a passing and rushing touchdown in his first NFL appearance and securing the 24-3 victory. Staubach completed seven of 15 passes for 220 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. His performance was far from a complete takeover of the starting position, but the athleticism, deep passing and improvisational ability that would define his career were already visible. This game belongs on the countdown because it marked the first appearance of one of the most important players in franchise history. Staubach did not become Dallas’ permanent starter until 1971, but his debut offered an unmistakable preview. The Cowboys had found a very special quarterback who would lead them into their championship era. #Cowboys vs #Cardinals 1969 The Roger Staubach Era begins Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 24, St. Louis Cardinals 3 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/KsZk56ehCF — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 19, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Staubach’s first ever NFL completion would be that 75-yard touchdown pass to Rentzel, making the play both memorable and inspirational to all of Cowboys nation. title: 3 losers from Cowboys fight-filled scrimmage against Saints
summary: Tuesday was supposed to be a rather significant date on the Cowboys training camp calendar, their second and final joint practice/scrimmage opportunity to continue sorting out the depth chart with invaluable live reps against another opponent. Dallas came into this scrimmage with plenty of depth chart questions following their first preseason game, but one of […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 23: Donovan Ezeiruaku #41 of the Dallas Cowboys runs across the field during an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tuesday was supposed to be a rather significant date on the Cowboys training camp calendar, their second and final joint practice/scrimmage opportunity to continue sorting out the depth chart with invaluable live reps against another opponent. Dallas came into this scrimmage with plenty of depth chart questions following their first preseason game, but one of the only big ways the depth sorted itself out on Tuesday was due to players putting themselves in a negative light by being involved in one or more of several fights that broke out on the day. Having already looked at three winners on a day that will go down as mostly useless because of these fights, unfortunately the skirmishing has to remain a topic for a bit longer as it also helps frames our three losers on the day – with injuries also having some say. 1. EDGE Donovan Ezeiruaku It really was not all that long ago that nearly the entire hopes of the Cowboys generating a pass rush in 2026 seemingly rested on the shoulders of second-year draft pick Donovan Ezeiruaku, who had a promising rookie campaign despite being in horrible circumstances for the defense as a whole in 2025. Good on the Cowboys for adding Rashan Gary since this time, Malachi Lawrence in the draft, and then earlier this week Von Miller as well, but the reason we now have to feel much better about these veteran additions instead of continuing to hype up Ezeiruaku still feels yucky. For the second time this training camp, Ezeiruaku was told to hit the showers early for fighting, this time throwing a punch at a Saints player. Just before this video began, Donovan Ezeiruaku tried to take on the whole Saints roster pic.twitter.com/m3o1M6zOZ1 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 18, 2026 Availability is the best ability any player can have, so it is highly concerning that Ezeiruaku is not even exhibiting the ability to be available for as many reps as needed, even in practice settings. Dallas’ number one concern coming out of the preseason win over the Seahawks on defense should be how well they can set the edge from their outside linebacker position. The Miller acquisition was an awesome immediate response to get better in this area even after just one preseason game, but in order to keep the upside of this veteran addition high, the Cowboys need their young talent to come along on the edge as well. Ezeiruaku is supposed to be the cream of the crop in this regard, but now has a potential mountain (or at least a decent hill) to climb just to be back in the good graces of this coaching staff. 2. RB Jaydon Blue Sticking with the availability trend, RB2 candidate Jaydon Blue has hit hard times ever since the Seahawks game. The Cowboys saw other depth in the backfield pop in the game, and upon return to Oxnard, have not even been able to put Blue on the field. Blue was not a full participant at practice on Monday, and then did not participate in the scrimmage on Tuesday. Jaydon Blue (shoulder) didn't practice today in #Cowboys practice vs. Saints. unknown if he'll be cleared vs. Cardinals on Saturday, but something to keep an eye on. — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 18, 2026 Time is ticking rapidly at this point when it comes to the amount of practice and game reps combined the Cowboys will be able to use to decide their pecking order at running back. Just for the moment the amount of time Blue is missing is not a death-con level red alert, but if it starts to extend with the second preseason game looming on Saturday, there are more than enough hungry mouths to feed with Malik Davis, Israel Abanikanda, and a healing Phil Mafah to push Blue down the depth chart. To make matters worse was how the offense popped against the Saints on the practice fields at Oxnard. The pass offense absolutely lit it up, an area that Blue could have contributed and made a real difference in the backfield competition where he is undoubtedly the most natural pass catcher of the RB group at the moment. 3. TE Michael Trigg Another player that mainly finds himself on this list because he was not available for the scrimmage, UDFA TE Michael Trigg also could not contribute to the good day the Cowboys had through the air. Although he did so a little bit against the Seahawks, that was without Jake Ferguson playing at all, Luke Schoonmaker playing just eight snaps, and Brevyn Spann-Ford also not playing at all. This feels like the umpteenth training camp in a row where the tight end depth chart has a lot of intrigue and some roster longshot “pet cats”, but by about this time in the summer session, the realization that Ferguson is going to take up the vast majority of the space available for any other TEs to play is made. The Cowboys showed this by getting Ferguson involved in his usual red zone ways against the Saints, but also by getting creative with TE1. PA shovel to Jake Ferguson pic.twitter.com/2iUzaLMBQ6 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 18, 2026 Even Luke Schoonmaker got in on the action. Schoon hauls it in 👊 #CowboysCamp | @AmericanAir pic.twitter.com/oL1HPKZtXd — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 18, 2026 Just like favorite ice cream flavors, every Cowboys fan may still cling onto their favorite tight end beyond Ferguson to contribute to this offense in 2026, with two preseason games to go. With three receivers that demand seeing the field at a very high rate and Ferguson coming on stronger and stronger as camp progresses though, the team’s most experienced tight end was another winner on the day for Tuesday, and it makes the rest of the position group more of a loser. Trigg is the new undrafted player that wasn’t on the field at all in this practice, creating a gap for him to close right as the cream is starting to rise to the top all over the roster and more established players are showing their regular season form.

title: Cowboys straddle physicality vs undisciplined in Saints scrimmage
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are trying to establish a new identity in 2026. They’ve talked a lot about physicality and intensity. That’s a good thing, and not to sound “old school,” but it’s still part of a winning culture, even in 2026. But being physical and being undisciplined aren’t the same thing, and Tuesday, August 18, […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 4: Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys on the field during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 4, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are trying to establish a new identity in 2026. They’ve talked a lot about physicality and intensity. That’s a good thing, and not to sound “old school,” but it’s still part of a winning culture, even in 2026. But being physical and being undisciplined aren’t the same thing, and Tuesday, August 18, we saw the latter. At least seven altercations were documented between the two teams Tuesday; Cowboys defensive edge Donovan Ezeiruaku’s day was even cut short after one of the fights. The thing is, these fights just shouldn’t be happening, and seven of them in one day is a black eye for everybody involved. Nobody minds a little jawing at training camp. Football is an emotional sport, but there’s a difference between playing with an edge and letting that edge derail practice and possibly lead to injury or suspension. What if this happened in the regular season? This game is a game of inches, a game of detail, and losing your cool even for a moment could be the difference between getting cut or not, making the playoffs or not, and for players on the cusp of those consequences, throwing control away so freely could reveal a lot about the makeup of a team. Players should compete. Offensive linemen should finish blocks. Defensive backs should challenge receivers. Running backs shouldn’t shy away from contact, but once players start throwing punches or dragging teammates into confrontations, the competitive benefit disappears. A player who finishes a rep and walks away after getting into it with an opponent? That’s competitiveness. A player who starts throwing punches, gets ejected from practice, risks an injury and costs his teammates reps? That’s not toughness. That’s a lack of discipline, and there was plenty of that on display Tuesday, in contrast to the culture Dallas is trying to build now. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer acknowledged the intensity of the practice but made it clear that the fights weren’t what Dallas wanted to see. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer was not happy about all of the fights during today’s practice. Donovan Ezeiruaku was thrown out for throwing a punch pic.twitter.com/TVdFJe2GVy — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 18, 2026 The Cowboys shouldn’t dull their edge, they need it, but this edge without discipline is not toughness, it’s a liability. What’s your take on all the fights at the Cowboys/Saints scrimmage?

(Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The second preseason game of the year gets underway for the Dallas Cowboys on Saturday night, and you are going to want to have your pot of coffee ready as kickoff isn’t until 10 pm ET. Buckle up. As the preseason continues to roll on so do the unofficial depth charts. NFL teams are required to submit these in advance of preseason games, but they all highly stress the unofficial nature of them. Here is what the Cowboys have offered ahead of Saturday night’s tilt against the Arizona Cardinals. There are very few differences between the latest unofficial depth chart and the one that Dallas released before the preseason began last week . Obviously Von Miller is featured here, though. And the team seemingly forgot to remove the name of Traeshon Holden from the depth chart. The Cowboys still notably have some “or” designations at a handful of areas where roster battles are underway. They are between three different pairs of players: Joe Milton and Sam Howell Marist Liufau and Sam Williams Shavon Revel and Cobie Durant When it comes to these specific roster battles the only one that figures to be of critical nature is the one between Liufau and Williams. The pairs of Milton/Howell and Revel/Durant are more competing for placements on the roster where Liufau and Williams are likely contending for a single spot. The Von Miller signing somewhat underscores that a bit. What do you make of the second unofficial depth chart of the year? Let us know in the comments below.

summary: The Dallas Cowboys did not get nearly as much on-field work with live reps against another opponent as they would have expected, or head coach Brian Schottenheimer would have liked, in Tuesday’s joint practice against the New Orleans Saints from Oxnard. The overall most noteworthy thing that happened in the practice was an obscene number […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 4: Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 4, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys did not get nearly as much on-field work with live reps against another opponent as they would have expected, or head coach Brian Schottenheimer would have liked, in Tuesday’s joint practice against the New Orleans Saints from Oxnard. The overall most noteworthy thing that happened in the practice was an obscene number of skirmishes and fights, which put into jeopardy if the scrimmage would even make it until the end. It ultimately did, but by the time it got there, six or seven different fighting incidents made it hard to read through these bold red lines and find the real football things to talk about. Football things did indeed happen though, enough to pick out a winner each for both sides of the ball, as well as a third that oversaw it all. Here are Tuesday’s three winners against the Saints. 1. QB Dak Prescott Dak Prescott did throw an early interception in this practice, but bounced back to keep his name firmly near the top of most-consistent performers in a good way this training camp for the Cowboys. It is Prescott’s side of the ball where the Cowboys have some of their most experienced and outwardly competitive players, yet the expectation that any of these names will see real preseason playing time is still doubtful. Perhaps this circumstance served as a dash of extra motivation for the Cowboys offense to sling it all over the yard on Tuesday, because with Prescott at the helm they did just that. Dak Prescott with the true definition of a “F— it. George down there somewhere” ball pic.twitter.com/JR34He0N89 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 18, 2026 Some of Prescott’s top highlight plays came throwing to players that also did not see the field at all against the Seahawks, mainly George Pickens. It’s hard to understate how much the entire dynamic of this team can change on a dime once they have the element of Prescott throwing over the top for Pickens on an every-down basis, and thanks to Prescott’s accuracy there were reminders of this against the Saints. Dak Prescott is out here absolutely dealing today. 👀 this throw … nasty. 🫪 this catch from George Pickens… nasty. #Cowboys offense must be fed up or something. pic.twitter.com/01UbWfDolo — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 17, 2026 Prescott didn’t just stop at making sure Pickens got his work and looked good doing so, continuing to spread the ball around with elite “point guard” like efficiency, also throwing this touchdown to Ryan Flournoy and hitting Jake Ferguson throughout the afternoon as well. Dak to Ryan Flournoy pic.twitter.com/i3b0HPr7of — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 18, 2026 Tough Jake Ferguson grab pic.twitter.com/ytr8dV3btL — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 18, 2026 2. CB Reddy Steward As for the Cowboys defense coached up by Christian Parker, all eyes were yet again on the secondary where questions remain to be answered about who can separate themself at cornerback and safety. The best things the backend of this defense did as a group against the Seahawks was play strong on the perimeter in run support, as well as bounce back after allowing an opening drive touchdown to shut the Seahawks out for three quarters and change. There were flashes of all these same things in a scrimmage setting against the Saints, and one player popped in both coverage and run support alike, Reddy Steward. Isaiah Land with the *sack*, and then DaRon Bland tips the ball downfield and Reddy Steward grabs the INT. a beautiful sequence. the corners didn’t stop playing despite the would-be sack. #Cowboys — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 18, 2026 Steward had one of two interceptions on the day for the Dallas defense, even though the play in a real game would have likely been an Isiah Land sack instead. Steward also made this play weaving around a block to make a strong tackle against the run. the athleticism by Reddy Steward to avoid the blocker and make this play … #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/RACK6lZIe9 — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 18, 2026 In six of the Cowboys last seven games of 2025, Steward played at least half of the team’s defensive snaps. While this may not being saying a whole lot because of the ineptness of said defense, this deep into 2026 training camp, Steward is finding a way to lean on this experience and stand out with some regularity. Based off of Tuesday’s performance, he will be a player to circle for Saturday’s second preseason test at the Arizona Cardinals. 3. HC Brian Schottenheimer At first glance, it might seem a bit odd to put the head coach of a team involved with so many extra curricular activities during a scrimmage as a winner of the day, but yet here we are. When it comes to ways the Cowboys have been feeling and moving different from years past this offseason, Schottenheimer’s overall culture having another year to marinate is a big part of this. With the Cowboys – and Saints – both acting out of line for so much of the practice on Tuesday, it gives Schotty a chance to really put this culture to the test. The head coach said he was “disappointed in the work” on Tuesday because he didn’t think the team “got enough good work”, with “too many bodies on the ground” . Schotty later reiterated that the nature of the team’s remaining practices has to be better, and having the chance to set the tone as the leader that can help this team do so makes him a winner in some sense on the day. Handling adversity is something every team will have to go through in the regular season, and even that elusive postseason the Cowboys are more than aiming for this year, and right now Dallas gets a chance to “practice” of sorts what handling this may look like following the joint practice. It stands to reason the Cowboys will be hearing plenty from Schottenheimer about culture and standards in the coming days, and if this message is received as well as others that Schottenheimer has gotten through, Dallas will come out the other side of this a more cohesive and disciplined team in time for the games to really matter.

title: Cowboys news: Saints joint practice has multiple brawls
summary: The Cowboys and the Saints tried to have a joint practice. Player fights marred the day and prevented a real scrimmage rhythm to develop. The Dallas Cowboys have become the destination many superstars want to go to because of their notoriety. Von Miller chose Dallas for different reasons. Here is the latest news around the […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle Tommy Dunn Jr. (95) at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cowboys and the Saints tried to have a joint practice. Player fights marred the day and prevented a real scrimmage rhythm to develop. The Dallas Cowboys have become the destination many superstars want to go to because of their notoriety. Von Miller chose Dallas for different reasons. Here is the latest news around the Dallas Cowboys. Multiple brawls mar Saints-Cowboys joint practice session – Katherine Terrell, ESPN The Cowboys and Saints ended up spending as much time fighting as practicing on Tuesday. Saints center Erik McCoy tossed a helmet in one brawl, and in another, his own helmet was lost before he and Cowboys outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku threw punches. Ezeiruaku was thrown out of practice afterward for the second time this offseason. He threw a punch earlier in training camp and was sent to the locker room. He and Schottenheimer had a conversation after that dustup, and the coach said he will have another one with him. Brian Schottenheimer ‘disappointed’ with ‘chippy’ Cowboys-Saints joint practice – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys head coach wasn’t always pleased with the outcome of the joint practice. “A little chippy,” Schottenheimer said. “Not the way we like to do business. Got to be better, but I’ve got to look at the film. We’re certainly not going to take s— from anybody, but again, it was chippy on both sides. Like I’ve said, I want our guys to play on the edge without going over the edge. One guy sounds like he might’ve thrown a punch, and that’s why he left practice early.” Why Von Miller chose to live out his ‘dream’ of playing for the Cowboys – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com A relationship that felt like a long time coming—Von Miller wearing the star on his helmet. Miller sat down with Prescott and the two struck up a conversation, where Miller gave his perspective on the team Dallas had assembled ahead of the 2026 season. “Hey man, it’s about time, Dak,” Miller told him. “It’s about time. You’ve got to break through with one of these teams, you’ve got to break through one of these years. I think this year you’ll be able to do it. You’ve got everybody to do it.” Two areas Brian Schottenheimer wants the Cowboys to improve against Cardinals – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Despite the win against the Seattle Seahawks, the standard fell short in a few areas for Brian Schottenheimer. “Our mantra is get back to basics,” Schottenheimer said.”Got to pay more attention to detail. Very, very disappointed in how we lost contain. Very disappointed in how we gave up kick side leverage. And the ball’s supposed to be kept on your right shoulder? Keep it on your right shoulder. The ball’s supposed to be on your left shoulder? Keep it on your left shoulder.” Predicting Cowboys’ OLB depth chart after Von Miller addition – Brian Martin, Blogging the Boys How does the addition of Von Miller shake up the OLB room? The guess here is the Dallas Cowboys will carry six OLBs on the active 53-man roster this season with a couple more on the practice squad to be called up when/if needed. As things stand right now, we have Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku as the starter’s with Malachi Lawrence and now Von Miller as the primary backups. That leaves two spots up for grabs. Outside the top four, we have James Houston securing a roster spot as the fifth OLB on the depth chart right now. John Niland’s ‘triumphant’ life: Highs, lows and the ex-Cowboy’s fulfilling final chapter – Kevin Sherrington , Dallas Morning News The Cowboys community mourns the loss of John Niland, who passed away at 82 over the weekend. Of all the legendary linemen in all of the Cowboys ’ hallowed history, only three drew more first-team All-Pro or Pro Bowl honors than John Niland . Fifth pick of the ‘66 draft out of Iowa. Left guard on the Cowboys’ first Super Bowl champion. From left to right in front of Roger Staubach in that Super Bowl season it was Ralph Neely , Niland, Dave Manders, Blaine Nye and Rayfield Wright , the first great offensive line in the organization’s long history of such. Daily discussion question: What did you make of the scrimmage against the Saints?

title: Bo Nix excited about what the Broncos’ offense can accomplish this season
summary: Entering his third year as quarterback of the Denver Broncos, Bo Nix is poised for his best season yet. Through two seasons of play, the former first-round pick has put up some eye-popping numbers. Nix has thrown for 7,706 yards and 54 touchdowns. His mobility has also been an asset, reeling off 786 rushing yards […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL, CO - August 18 : Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix answers questions from reporters at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Tuesday, August 18, 2026. (Photo by Hyoung Chang/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Entering his third year as quarterback of the Denver Broncos, Bo Nix is poised for his best season yet. Through two seasons of play, the former first-round pick has put up some eye-popping numbers . Nix has thrown for 7,706 yards and 54 touchdowns. His mobility has also been an asset, reeling off 786 rushing yards and 9 touchdowns. In his 34 regular season starts, the Broncos’ signal caller has 24 wins to his name with eight fourth quarter comebacks and ten game-winning drives. There is no doubt Nix has some things to work on, but he has exceeded most any expectations any fan across Broncos Country could have had when he was taken with the 12th overall selection in the 2024 NFL Draft. Quite simply, he has been one of the most productive quarterbacks in the National Football League since being drafted. This season, Nix has a few more friends on offense. That’s a major reason he has a great chance to take his game to the next level in 2025. Earlier int the offseason, the Broncos’ brass made a bold move adding wide receiver Jaylen Waddle into the mix. Waddle’s dynamic playmaking ability is undeniable, and Nix is excited about what he will do for the team this season. “It’s been great. He’s an elite player, and he makes our room better. With him out there on the field, he adds a different level of explosiveness and just allows other guys to be better,” stated Nix. Alongside Waddle, the Broncos boast an extremely talented group of receivers. Courtland Sutton, the long-time veteran, will once again be a focal point of the offense’s aerial attack. After them, Troy Franklin, Pat Bryant, and Marvin Mims Jr. round out a five-deep corps at the position—arguably one of the most underrated in the league. It’s been a long time since the franchise has had so much talent at the position. This year, they have the potential to be special. Speaking of special, Nix’s spoke highly of Franklin after yesterday’s practice and believes he is in store for a big season. “Troy’s a guy that you don’t realize how much he’s actually picking up. You don’t realize how much he’s willing to learn. He asks great questions, very detailed questions. He definitely clears the air on a lot of things just by the questions he asks. He’s a very intelligent football player, underrated knowledge. I don’t think enough people know that about him,” remarked Nix whose relationship with Franklin goes back to 2022 when they first became teammates with the Oregon Ducks. “I think now in Year 3, he’s just putting his skill set with that knowledge that he’s learned and put together in the NFL. Now you can see he’s really starting to shine and really start being a play maker that we know he can be,” added Nix. But it’s not just the star power at wide receiver that has Nix excited. In the 2026 NFL Draft, the franchise drafted Jonah Coleman who has stood out since donning the orange and blue. Second-year running back RJ Harvey will be a big part of the team’s plans this season, and veteran J.K. Dobbins looked great in 2025 before he missed the latter portion of the injury due to injury. In their first preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons, the Broncos rushed for an impactful 162 yards on the ground. Their ability to tote the rock and control the pace of the game earned them a decisive victory. That sort of rushing attack will be crucial for the offense to reach new heights this season. “We have really good backs, and we’re going to be excited to use those guys coming out of the backfield, running the football. We’re excited about them and their skill set and then just grow on what we’ve been building over the training camp in this offseason.” This week, the Broncos host the Green Bay Packers in front of a hometown crowd for their second preseason game. It will be Nix’s first in-game reps since breaking his ankle in the team’s overtime win against the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Playoff round. While his reps will be limited, Nix is approaching the matchup just like he would any other game. “You treat it as a real one and treat it like you’re going to go play the whole entire game and then play with maximum intensity until they pull you.”

title: 4 Players the Denver Broncos should consider extending this year
summary: Let’s start off by congratulating all-time great Denver Bronco Von Miller on signing with the Dallas Cowboys. While I doubt I’ll be cheering to see his team win, I’ll definitely be cheering for our guy to have a successful season and rack up more sacks for his career. If the football gods are feeling feisty, […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - OCTOBER 26: Brandon Jones (22) and Riley Moss (21) of the Denver Broncos celebrate a pass break up intended for KaVontae Turpin (9) of the Dallas Cowboys during the fourth quarter at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver on Sunday, October 26, 2025. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Let’s start off by congratulating all-time great Denver Bronco Von Miller on signing with the Dallas Cowboys. While I doubt I’ll be cheering to see his team win, I’ll definitely be cheering for our guy to have a successful season and rack up more sacks for his career. If the football gods are feeling feisty, they could cause a lot of belly-ache in Broncos Country by having this season end in a Broncos vs Cowboys Super Bowl… I was curious to see what kind of deal Von would get in Dallas, and it got me to thinking about the Broncos cap situation in 2026. Currently, according to overthecap.com, the Broncos have ~$36M in cap space. That’s a lot of flexibility for the team, but I honestly can’t for the life of me think of a free agent they should look at bringing in. So the next logical thing to look at is who on this team the Broncos could extend and put some of that cap space to use on? The list of UFAs in 2027 is quite long , but here are the guys I’m thinking are worth a look at extending sooner rather than later: Ja’Quan McMillian – Ja’Quan is a flat-out playmaker. He’s deserving of a 3-4 year deal and a guy that I’d love to see retire as a Bronco. Riley Moss – Unless you are planning on letting him hit free agency and sliding Jahdae Barron into his starting spot, this is a deal that has to be done. Moss is a hell of a player and is another guy that hasn’t hit his ceiling yet. Marvin Mims – Mims has been a true weapon for this team as a returner, and he’s not stopped growing as a receiver. Even with the WR room thicker with talent, Mims is a playmaker who has real clutch ability. Brandon Jones – He’s a superb safety, and if the coaches think he has a couple years left in the tank, that’s an easy extension to get done that shouldn’t break the bank. Now that the Broncos aren’t burdened with expensive dead money from bad choices in the past, they are able to strategically put the cap to use and extend players early instead of late, which should save money in the long run. If you could extend any two of the above options next week, who would it be? Let us know in the comments who you think is worth a deal right now. title: NFL players are now suing to have the option for NCAA eligibility
summary: Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reported earlier today that there are current NFL players who are looking to be granted an extra year of college football eligibility. If you haven’t been following the news at the college level, the NCAA has granted a five-year eligibility agreement to close some of the loopholes that allowed players […]
full_text: BATON ROUGE, LA - OCTOBER 11: Jack Pyburn #44 of the LSU Tigers in action against the South Carolina Gamecoks on October 11, 2025 at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images) Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reported earlier today that there are current NFL players who are looking to be granted an extra year of college football eligibility. If you haven’t been following the news at the college level, the NCAA has granted a five-year eligibility agreement to close some of the loopholes that allowed players to play six, seven, eight and even nine years of college ball due to various forms of redshirts. Since that announcement, players from the 2022 class, whose college eligibility has expired since they weren’t given that fifth year, have been making their case to return to college football for one more season, with the argument being that they should also benefit from this rule. Before Zenitz’s reporting, these players had mostly been players who at most had tryouts with NFL teams, but had not signed an NFL contract. The difference now is that some players under NFL contracts are looking to go back to college and cash in on some NIL money. The first official case of this seems to be former LSU edge rusher Jack Byburn, who signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as an undrafted free agent for $115,000 in guarantees. If Byburn is released from the Buccaneers at the cutdown deadline, he should be able to pocket that $115,000 without the team being able to claw it back, since he was released from the 53-man roster — even if he’s allowed to go the college route instead of re-signing to an NFL practice squad. Again, this is pending the courts ruling in his favor. New: Former #LSU Edge Jack Pyburn and current Tampa Bay Buccaneers DE filed a lawsuit today against the NCAA seeking a preliminary injunction that would give him the option to return to college. Sources tell me, @mzenitz , & @chris_hummer . https://t.co/hSwRHcRBhT pic.twitter.com/xzwwbkbxvH — AYS Sports (@AYSSPORTS) August 19, 2026 If you’re wondering, “Which Packers players were members of the 2022 recruiting class,” I took the time to figure that out. Below are all of the players on Green Bay’s roster who might be impacted if Pyburn receives a ruling from the courts to have the option to return to NCAA football. RB Damien Martinez WR Matthew Golden DL Chris McClellan EDGE Dani Dennis-Sutton EDGE Nyjalik Kelly CB Domani Jackson K Trey Smack Rookie Brandon Cisse is actually a member of the 2023 class, which means he would have had two extra years of eligibility if he had returned to school, but it’s worth noting that he declared for the draft early and didn’t have his eligibility expire naturally. If 2022 class players (or later) are allowed to return to the NCAA for a fifth year, only if they didn’t declare early for the league, here’s the relevant Packers, since both Martinez and Golden also declared for the draft early: DL Chris McClellan EDGE Dani Dennis-Sutton EDGE Nyjalik Kelly CB Domani Jackson K Trey Smack McClellan, Dennis-Sutton, Jackson and Smack are likely to make the Packers’ 53-man roster, so it’s unlikely that they would test the college route, even if it opens up. The interesting one is Kelly, who will still make a guaranteed $262,500 from Green Bay if he is released at the cutdown deadline — which the team wouldn’t be able to claw back upon his release. Potentially, he could double-dip and take that money while returning to college football, depending on what the courts allow. An NFL practice squad salary for a first-year player is a fixed rate of $13,750 per week ($247,500 for the full season), for perspective. According to an ESPN article recently posted by reporter Max Olson, the average cost of a starting edge defender for one year at the college level for “Power 4” programs is between $500,000 and $1.2 million. For Kelly, specifically, how a judge rules on Pyburn’s situation could be a major factor in whether it makes financial sense to go back to the college route for another year. — Update: Three Ole Miss players who had their eligibility expire from the 2022 class and signed with NFL teams this offseason have been granted a temporary retraining order for a fifth year of eligibility in college, per ESPN . Those players are tight end Dae’Quan Wright (currently of the Cleveland Browns), defensive lineman Zxavian Harris (who was a member of the New Orleans Saints) and safety Wydett Williams Jr. (currently of the Arizona Cardinals). According to ESPN, 33 athletes, over multiple sports, filed a lawsuit in Louisiana today. The only other current NFL player involved in that particular lawsuit is Anthony Hankerson, a running back for the Seattle Seahawks. Pyburn is joining the suit, per Dan Murphy and Pete Thamel’s reporting.

title: Packers Training Camp Recap: Cornerback and offensive line competitions are a full go
summary: Today marked the final practice the Green Bay Packers have before their travel day tomorrow, as they’ll play the Denver Broncos on Friday. Per head coach Matt LaFleur yesterday, the plan is for starters to play two drives against the Broncos, which is expected to be their last preseason opportunity. In Week 3, the Packers […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - SEPTEMBER 21: Green Bay Packers offensive tackle Jordan Morgan (77), Green Bay Packers guard Sean Rhyan (75), Green Bay Packers guard Elgton Jenkins (74), Green Bay Packers guard Aaron Banks (65), and Green Bay Packers offensive tackle Rasheed Walker (63) at the line of scrimmage during the first quarter of the National Football League game between the Green Bay Packers and Cleveland Browns on September 21, 2025, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Today marked the final practice the Green Bay Packers have before their travel day tomorrow, as they’ll play the Denver Broncos on Friday. Per head coach Matt LaFleur yesterday , the plan is for starters to play two drives against the Broncos, which is expected to be their last preseason opportunity. In Week 3, the Packers will use their starters in joint practices, but use their backups in their preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at Lambeau Field. Today’s practice was closed to the public but open to the media. It was also a half-speed “jogthrough” practice, so I’d put less emphasis on individual performances and more on the rotations the Packers used throughout the day. Injuries Good sign that Aaron Banks (knee) is practicing again after doing team yesterday for the first time. pic.twitter.com/lPdHzSdias — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) August 19, 2026 The Packers’ physically unable to perform list remains the same, with tight end Luke Musgrave (neck), edge defender Micah Parsons (knee), defensive lineman Jordon Riley (ankle) and long snapper Matt Orzech (calf) still inactive. Several players did return to practice today, though: receiver Bo Melton (stinger), edge defender Dani Dennis-Sutton (illness) and edge defender Nyjalik Kelly (knee). According to LaFleur, Dennis-Sutton overheated at practice, which put him into a medical protocol. Melton dropped out of practice yesterday, but it looks like he’s already good to go. The only players to miss practice, beyond the PUP list guys, were tackle Darian Kinnard (ankle) and safety Javon Bullard (foot). As a reminder, the team has described both of those injuries as short-term, and Bullard even stated that he’d be playing in games with his bone bruise if it were a game week. Offense The big question everyone has right now on offense is who will be starting on the line in Week 1 of the regular season. With Aaron Banks and Zach Bako-Bewele back in practice full-time now, the contenders for starting spots are all finally healthy at the same time. So what did the line look like today? A bunch of different combinations. The line started with Jordan Morgan, Banks, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk and Bako-Bewele (left to right), but there were several other iterations with the first-team unit on Wednesday. Monk also played center, Jager Burton played both left and right guard and Anthony Belton played right tackle. It seems like the only option that the Packers have ruled out is Belton playing right guard, for whatever reason. If you want a look at how Bank and Monk played in the preseason, we clipped up all of their snaps versus the Steelers (and split them by run and pass reps) for you. Defense On defense, the “starting” defensive linemen in the Packers’ 3-4 look were Jonathan Ford at nose tackle and Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks at the ends. With that being said, Javon Hargrave has been rotating in with the first-team unit, too, and has been regularly getting “first-look” opportunities when the team is in nickel sets. The biggest question, though, is at cornerback. Yesterday, it felt like the cornerback competition truly opened up for the first time, not just for the spot opposite Keisean Nixon — which had been the case throughout camp — but also Nixon’s spot (left cornerback) itself. Today was no different, as Nixon, Carrington Valentine, Brandon Cisse and Benjamin St-Juste were all heavily rotated in and out of the lineup with the 1s. Previously, Valentine and Cisse mostly battled for playing time opposite Nixon, while St-Juste was by far fourth in the pecking order. 11-on-11 starts w Banks & Monk at G, Cisse & Nixon at CB. Hadden at nickel. Monk rotates in at C, Burton at RG. — Mike Spofford (@mikespofford) August 19, 2026 The other position to watch is slot defender, where the Packers are looking for an answer behind the currently injured Bullard. Johnathan Baldwin was their preferred backup for most of the spring and summer, but he’s since been waived with an injury designation. Neither safety Kitan Oladapo nor cornerback Jaylin Simpson did well in the slot in their opportunity in the preseason opener. Since then, cornerback Kamal Hadden has returned to practice from injury, and he’s now getting most of the first-team snaps in the slot with Bullard out. Worth noting: Hadden picked off third-string quarterback Kyle McCord today, even if practice wasn’t at full speed. If he (and draft pick Domani Jackson) perform well enough, maybe the team keeps six cornerbacks on the 53-man roster.

title: For better or worse, Keisean Nixon is central to Packers DB plans
summary: Keisean Nixon is going to be a big part of the Packers’ defense in 2026. Whether you view that as a promise or a threat is up to you, but it’s true either way. Nixon, for all his foibles and follies in training camp this year, is essentially a load-bearing piece of the Packers’ secondary. […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Keisean Nixon #25 of the Green Bay Packers in action during the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Keisean Nixon is going to be a big part of the Packers’ defense in 2026. Whether you view that as a promise or a threat is up to you, but it’s true either way. Nixon, for all his foibles and follies in training camp this year, is essentially a load-bearing piece of the Packers’ secondary. There’s simply no other solution for the Packers. And there may never have been, for that matter. Free agency this year was not precisely awash with cornerback talent. Alontae Taylor was the big winner this spring, parlaying a moderately successful 2025 season with the Saints into a three-year, $58 million offer from the Titans. Jaylen Watson was just a bit behind him, putting four solid but overall undistinguished years with the Chiefs on tape and earning a three-year $51 million contract in Los Angeles as a result. Cordale Flott (Titans), Jamel Dean (Steelers), and Eric Stokes (yes, that one)(Steelers), rounded out the rest of the big spending, all signing deals averaging more than $10 million per year. To say nothing of the cap machinations necessary to make those deals happen in Green Bay, I don’t think any of those are going to move the needle for a fan base frustrated with Nixon, and that’s before we’ve even addressed potential fit questions. You need elite long speed to succeed in a scheme like Jonathan Gannon’s, which eliminates Watson (4.51 in the 40) and Flott (4.52) as options. And unless you want another go at the Eric Stokes experience, that leaves Taylor and Dean as options. Both of them can run, but Dean is already entering his age 30 season and is well beyond the typical age cliff for cornerbacks, and Taylor is, well, not very good. The Packers were reportedly in touch with former Seattle Seahawks cornerback Tariq Woolen, but he opted for a one-year $12 million deal with the Eagles. Given what we know about how the Packers tend to do business, the contract length was probably the sticking point; it seems safe to assume they’d probably want a longer contract. They don’t usually like to set themselves up to pay the same guy just a year into the future. The Packers did sign Benjamin St-Juste, who’s been successful in small doses in schemes like Gannon’s, but seems suited primarily for special teams at this point in his career. As far as roster construction goes, it seems like that’s about as well as the Packers could have done in free agency: a solid teams guy with some background in the scheme. So that’s free agency. What about the draft? Consensus opinion seems to indicate the talent at cornerback dropped off right around where the Packers were picking. In short, it was Brandon Cisse or bust. To this point, Cisse seems to have held up his end of the bargain. He’s been good, looks like a lock for the starting lineup, and has done everything asked of him. In the draft, at least, it looks like the Packers did about as well as they could. That doesn’t add up to a cornerback room designed to push Nixon out — or push him much of anywhere, for that matter. The Packers came into the offseason with Nixon and Carrington Valentine as their top two corners, and they exited it having added a promising rookie and a guy likely to play primarily special teams reps. What of the supposed competition at cornerback, then? Matt LaFleur’s comments about Nixon being in a competition are, in my eyes, a bit overblown. The Packers want to have a competitive camp; everybody does. But game it out — what happens as a result of this competition? Is Nixon actually going to be playing reserve reps when the season comes around? And, just as importantly, who’s playing instead of him? It’s probably not St-Juste, who wasn’t a full-time player for the Chargers last year and hasn’t played more than 77% of the snaps in a given year since 2023. And if it’s Carrington Valentine? Well, I guess just get ready to find/replace all of your pre-loaded complaints about Nixon with Valentine’s name, because everything people dislike about Nixon also applies to Valentine, and some of it is even worse. He, too, has inconsistent ball skills. He, too, is an inconsistent tackler ( just ask Dallas Goedert ). If Valentine lands in a bigger role, the most likely outcome is fans developing a strange, sudden respect for Nixon. That’s why, for better or for worse, we’re stuck with Nixon, and while not ideal, it’s probably about as good as it can get right now. The bottom line, though, is that this situation shouldn’t really be about Nixon at all. Sure, he’s been inconsistent in camp so far, but his belief remains unlimited, as it should. No defensive back should be anything other than infinitely confident in his own abilities. Nixon is just playing to his nature. The question, then, is who let it get to this point. Even if there was little else they could have done this spring, the Packers have been in a position where Nixon has been their best, if not only, option at corner for at least two seasons. If we want to point fingers, it seems like that’s not really Nixon’s fault at all. Every criticism thrown his way should maybe be directed toward the string of decisions that led to him being in this position at all. But that’s much harder to fit into an angry tweet.

title: What kind of run game do the Packers actually want?
summary: The Green Bay Packers seem to be in a state of continual flux on the offensive line lately. Last season, the team appeared to be moving in the direction of a bigger, power-focused line, but the summer of 2026 suggests that the rubber band is snapping back a bit in favor of a more athletic […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Jager Burton #52 of the Green Bay Packers in action during the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers seem to be in a state of continual flux on the offensive line lately. Last season, the team appeared to be moving in the direction of a bigger, power-focused line, but the summer of 2026 suggests that the rubber band is snapping back a bit in favor of a more athletic group that is more typical of the lines the Packers have fielded in recent decades. Dating back to Ted Thompson’s tenure as the team’s general manager, the Packers have generally prioritized agility and movement skills in their linemen over pure bulk, size, and brute strength. Combined with running backs whose abilities were also more centered around agility and a more pass-focused attack, this made for a good approach. However, the signs were all there that the team was looking to change that approach in 2025. The first indicator was the signing of guard Aaron Banks as a free agent. The second was drafting Anthony Belton in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Both players have body types that didn’t fit the typical mold of a Packers lineman; that mold had typically maxed out around 315 pounds and, again, focused on players who can move well in space. In contrast, Banks is 6-foot-5 and 325 pounds, while Belton goes 6-foot-6 and is listed at 336. While Banks started every game, Belton eventually moved into the starting lineup at right guard for the latter portion of the season. With Sean Rhyan (6-5, 321) moving from right guard to center after Elgton Jenkins’ injury, that was a heck of a lot of beef in the middle of the line. However, in training camp, both Banks and Belton have been in and out of the lineup at guard, with rookie Jager Burton (6-4, 312) and Jacob Monk (6-3, 308) getting much of the work at left and right guard, respectively, in the last week and a half or so. Banks has yet to take a snap in team drills, while Belton has been playing right tackle almost exclusively amid Zach Bako-Bewele’s gradual return from his own injury. The line that the Packers have been trotting out lately (with Bako-Bewele at tackle) would represent a substantial size difference compared to the unit that finished out last season. To that end, here’s a look at the average height/weight of the starting line in week one last year, the line that finished out the season in 2025, and the potential 2026 line (all numbers from Combine measurements): Line Players Avg. Height Avg. Weight 2025 Week 1 Walker, Banks, Jenkins, Rhyan, Tom 6 feet, 4.875 inches 314.6 lbs 2025 Wild Card Walker, Banks, Rhyan, Belton, Morgan 6 feet, 5.325 inches 321.2 lbs 2026 (possible) Morgan, Burton, Rhyan, Monk, Bako-Bewele 6 feet, 4.2 inches 311.2 lbs If the Packers end up rolling with the youngsters on the interior, they would be down by 10 pounds and more than an inch in height on average compared to the starting line at the end of last season. Unsurprisingly, Burton and Monk tested out much better than Banks and Belton did, with exceptional speed and athleticism RAS scores for their positions compared to just moderate ones for last year’s starters. This all comes back to the question in the headline of this piece: what do the Packers actually want their run game to be this season? That decision might actually hinge on the status of starting running back Josh Jacobs. Fundamentally, Jacobs is a power runner who is not particularly suited to outside zone. Building a bigger, people-moving line in front of a back like Jacobs makes sense, but if the Packers aren’t likely to have him around for much longer (which they’re not, one way or another), it stands to reason that they would start to transition away from that approach. A back like MarShawn Lloyd, who is more athletic and has better acceleration than Jacobs, could be better suited for an outside zone-heavy running game, which would clearly be a fit for the more athletic players like Burton and Monk. Belton has seemingly fallen out of favor with the coaches at guard. Matt LaFleur’s recent comments about Burton — saying that the rookie is making the coaching staff’s decisions “extremely difficult” — indicate that he’s very much in play for a starting spot. And Banks’ injury further complicates matters, preventing the team from getting a look at the interior group that finished out last season. Are the Packers preparing for life post-Jacobs by moving back towards a more movement-based run game? Or is this simply a function of injuries forcing the coaching staff’s hand? Time will tell, but don’t be too surprised if the concepts the team uses in the run game and the distribution of carries between Jacobs and Lloyd both end up tracking closely with the lineup on the interior of the offensive line.

title: Packers Film Room, Preseason Week 1: Nyjalik Kelly
summary: The Green Bay Packers have played their first preseason game and have their second one coming up. Before that second game hits, we’re going to try to hit a handful of these mini film rooms and look and individual players. Today, we’re looking at Nyjalik Kelly. Kelly signed with the Packers this spring as an […]
full_text: Green Bay Packers edge rusher Nyjalik Kelly (47) is shown during the first day of training camp Wednesday, July 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. It is the first of three consecutive public practices. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Green Bay Packers have played their first preseason game and have their second one coming up. Before that second game hits, we’re going to try to hit a handful of these mini film rooms and look and individual players. Today, we’re looking at Nyjalik Kelly. Kelly signed with the Packers this spring as an undrafted free agent out of the University of Central Florida. I’m not going to talk about him as a prospect, because the great Jon Meerdink already did that . You should absolutely read Jon’s profile if you haven’t already, but the big takeaways are this: long-armed athlete with great explosive grades in his RAS score. Nyjalik Kelly is a DE prospect in the 2026 draft class. He scored a 7.87 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 446 out of 2085 DE from 1987 to 2026. Pending Pro Day. https://t.co/OyyWryDmK1 pic.twitter.com/wMB5TkO5Js — RAS.football (@MathBomb) March 19, 2026 His best path to make the roster is as a pass rusher. His flashes in college were good, though he was a bit inconsistent. Here are a handful of notes I jotted down as I went through his snaps. Our own Justis Mosqueda charted the day and had Nyjalik Kelly with 10 snaps as the Edge Defender with the Packers second team defense . As far as a player and usage, Kelly looks like a typical Wide-9 rusher at this early point in his career. That is to say, he will line up outside of the widest player on the line and rush the passer or set the edge. Kelly has a wide array of moves, but he doesn’t appear to have a clear plan snap-to-snap. Sometimes it seems like he’s just throwing every move at the wall to see what lands. “How about a cross-chop? Maybe a Eurostep? A spin? Any of those work?” It’s cool to see those options in his arsenal, but he doesn’t really have an attack plan. Beyond that, there’s a tentativeness to his game at the moment. A false step before launching. A feeling-out period against an offensive tackle that leaves him a tick slow in his rep. That’s something that can get better simply with more reps, so maybe that improves as the preseason rolls on. It’s something to keep an eye on. He bites on a lot of misdirection as well. I don’t want to say he doesn’t seem to know where the ball is, but that seems to be the case at times. Again, that’s something that could improve with more reps. The transition from college to the NFL is tough for any player. Right now, it looks like he’s so dialed into doing whatever his assignment is on the play that he’s not always tuned into what’s going on around him. We’ll close out with a couple of nice things I saw from him. The strength and recognition isn’t always on display (for the reasons outlined above), but when it shows up, it’s pretty nice. This next clip shows a run play with Kelly on the right side of the screen (#47) in a four-point stance. He takes on the tackle, stands him up, then sheds and takes down the ballcarrier. That’s on display again in this next clip, knocking back the tight end and shedding to make the tackle (right side of the screen). You can see the jolt in his hands in this next clip, knocking back the tight end on the left side. On the right side of the screen, you can see his speed & burst off the line, and his dip to get under the tackle. On the left side, you can see his long arms at work, with a one-arm attack against the tackle before dipping underneath on a straight path to the QB. He knocks knees & is tripped up on his way to the sack, but that initial approach shows some real promise. Kelly has an intriguing skillset. It’s not hard to look at the flashes and see something that could be useful in a somewhat limited capacity this upcoming season. Plus, I’m no special teams maven, but it seems like a dude with long arms could be useful in that area of the game. Still, he’s far from a refined player. I’m curious to watch him through the next two preseason games to see what he looks like. Albums listened to: Phoebe Bridgers – Lost Weekend ; John Carpenter – Cathedral

title: Josh Jacobs suspension still on the table but uncertain following May arrest
summary: It has been nearly three months since Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs was arrested on charges of felony strangulation and several other misdemeanors related to domestic abuse. That’s also just about how long it’s been since we last had an update from the team, the league, or law enforcement officials. Jacobs has said via […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers looks on during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images It has been nearly three months since Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs was arrested on charges of felony strangulation and several other misdemeanors related to domestic abuse. That’s also just about how long it’s been since we last had an update from the team, the league, or law enforcement officials. Jacobs has said via his lawyers that he “vehemently denies the allegations”. Meanwhile, h ead coach Matt LaFleur echoed the team’s initial statement, saying they would let the process play out. Aaaaand, now we’re in the back half of August. The NFL recently announced its first round of player suspensions for 2026, most notably for Atlanta Falcons DE James Pearce, who was suspended 8 games after his February arrest on domestic violence charges which included stalking and aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. No suspension was announced for Jacobs, likely because things are still under investigation. If or when things finally start moving again, I don’t have high hopes that the league will respond in a way I deem appropriate. After all, stalking and aggravated battery get you 8 games. Holding a gun to someone’s head will cost you 5 games. Sometimes domestic violence incidents get you suspended for 6 games . Or 4 games. But hey! Sometimes domestic violence does get you kicked out of the league , but I suspect that’s only if you’re not very good at your job. Pretty soon they’re going to let players spin a big wheel to decide their fate just like on The Price is Right . Back to Josh Jacobs. With the most recent update being that there…is no update, ESPN’s Adam Schefter says that a suspension for Jacobs is still on the table. As evidenced by the examples above, it’s looking like Jacobs could be facing a punishment anywhere from a 1 game suspension to being completely banned from the league. The NFL just doesn’t know.

For an offense that is entering its second year under […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 18: Jayden Higgins #81 of the Houston Texans looks on as he takes the field prior to an NFC Divisional Playoff game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on January 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. For an offense that is entering its second year under offensive coordinator Nick Caley and trying to match the defense in terms of firepower, losing Jayden Higgins is a critical blow to their depth chart. Higgins, soon to turn 24 on December 15th, was drafted in the second round (34th overall) by the Houston Texans last year in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Iowa State. Much like his current Texans’ teammate and former Iowa State Cyclone Xavier Hutchinson, Higgins possesses the speed, agile feet, and length that makes him a triple threat on the field and an ideal NFL wide receiver. He only had a handful targets at the beginning of the 2025 season, but by midseason, his ease at getting open had made him a favorite target of both Davis Mills and C.J. Stroud. In his rookie season last year, Higgins tallied (including playoffs): 19 Games (11 Starts) 50 Recs on 82 Tgts (61 Ctch%) 623 Yards (12.5 Y/R) 6 TDs 768 Offensive Snaps; 70.0 PFF Grade #texans WR Jayden Higgins suffered a torn ACL per source. This is a massive blow to a young and talented WR room on a Super Bowl contending roster. Higgins had taken a huge jump entering year two in Houston's eyes. He was going to play inside and outside and could impact all 3… — James Palmer (@JamesPalmerTV) August 19, 2026 Rookie Jayden Higgins highlights Buy stock now pic.twitter.com/cCj91RW4uQ — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) July 23, 2026 After catching five passes for 42 yards and a touchdown during Houston’s comeback win against the Jacksonville Jaguars in week 9 last year, Jayden Higgins had fully earned the trust of his quarterbacks and his coaching staff. He would go on start five of the final eight games of that season, converting multiple crucial downs for both Mills and Stroud, and got touchdown passes against the Buffalo Bills, the L. A. Chargers, and the Indianapolis Colts in the regular season-finale. Nico Collins spoke the truth when he stated Higgins had, “…all the tools in the world” during training camp a few weeks ago, and Houston will be very hard pressed to find a replacement of his caliber. Nico Collins on Jayden Higgins: “That boy a dog. Got all the tools in the world. Dude is gunna be the face of this franchise one year. His playmaking ability, his size, he got all the tools in the world. I can’t wait to see him rock out this year, it’s gunna be exciting.” pic.twitter.com/V7wp7QVsUw — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) August 2, 2026 With Higgins now out, Houston will rely more heavily on #1 receiver Nico Collins, returning receiver Tank Dell, and backups Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel, Justin Watson, Jared Wayne, and rookie sixth-round pick Lewis Bond. In fact, with Higgins now set to be placed on injured reserve, ending his 2026 NFL season, Houston will likely be searching for a tall, agile receiver to take his routes, meaning a competition between Hutchinson, Watson, and Wayne is likely to ensue in the following days. While it is devastating news, we all will be patiently waiting for 2027 in anticipation to see Jayden Higgins get wide open in the end-zone for a Texans touchdown yet again. Even though it would have been nice to see him on the field while the team guns for its first Super Bowl, we hope that Jayden Higgins is able to recover quickly and be back to his regular NFL form by training camp next year. But, until then, it’s the next man up! Who do you think will fill in Higgins’ role on the squad? I have a feeling we’ll be seeing a whole lot more Xavier Hutchinson this season, now, but with how good Jared Wayne looked in his limited action last week against the Chargers, I could be very wrong. Let us know your thoughts down in the comments below! Go Texans!

title: Colts reportedly receive positive news on TE Tyler Warren’s groin injury
summary: According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz, the Indianapolis Colts have received positive news on Tyler Warren’s groin injury suffered during Wednesday’s joint training camp practice against the Atlanta Falcons at Grand Park: The Colts’ 2nd-year tight end left Wednesday’s practice during 11-on-11 drills against the Falcons defense, returning in uniform (albeit without a helmet), but […]

(Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz, the Indianapolis Colts have received positive news on Tyler Warren’s groin injury suffered during Wednesday’s joint training camp practice against the Atlanta Falcons at Grand Park: Sources: #Colts TE Tyler Warren suffered an abductor strain during practice today, but in the words of a source, he “is going to be fine” and is not expected to miss much time, if any. Great news. pic.twitter.com/XvbQptvoRo — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) August 20, 2026 The Colts’ 2nd-year tight end left Wednesday’s practice during 11-on-11 drills against the Falcons defense, returning in uniform (albeit without a helmet), but with a wrap and ice on his injured groin along the sidelines. He rightfully did not return to the practice field again and will presumably be shut down for Thursday’s training camp practice finale, as well as all of preseason—if that wasn’t already a foregone conclusion. The Colts avoided a potential critical injury, as Warren is expected to be featured prominently within their first-team offense, even with the new addition of veteran wideout Keenan Allen along the outside. Their 2025 first round pick has already flashed again throughout this year’s training camp and is coming off an impressive rookie season in which he recorded 76 receptions for 817 total receiving yards and 4 touchdown receptions, as well as rushed for another score. He’s poised to have a potential breakout 2nd-year campaign in Indianapolis. It sounds like Warren will be out a ‘week,’ which is great, since it’s not ‘weeks.’ The latter could’ve been devastating for an offense where he’s expected to be one of the leading targets, and that could also potentially be without Alec Pierce to begin the 2026 regular season. Simply put, starting Colts quarterback Daniel Jones needs his big bodied, security blanket out there!

title: Colts CB Justin Walley returns favor with pick-six in joint-practice against Falcons
summary: WESTFIELD, Ind. — Indianapolis Colts cornerback Justin Walley found himself on both ends of highlight-reel plays during Wednesday’s joint-practice with the Atlanta Falcons, but it was the second-year nickel who got the last laugh in the final team session. Earlier on the opposite practice field, it was receiver Drake London who made a sensational snag […]
full_text: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Justin Walley jumps a pass to pick off Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa for a pick-six during the training camp joint-practice at Droplight Grand Park Sports Campus — August 19, 2026. | Stampede Blue Staff WESTFIELD, Ind. — Indianapolis Colts cornerback Justin Walley found himself on both ends of highlight-reel plays during Wednesday’s joint-practice with the Atlanta Falcons, but it was the second-year nickel who got the last laugh in the final team session. Earlier on the opposite practice field, it was receiver Drake London who made a sensational snag over Walley while backpedaling before he took off for the end zone. The Falcons’ 6-foot-4 receiver raised his arms to veritably ‘Moss’ the 5-foot-10 Walley on the far sideline, reaching high enough to haul in the catch. Both teams had an opportunity in the final 11-on-11 session to move the ball the length of the field. On the second play of the Falcons’ offensive series, quarterback Tua Tagovailoa held the ball a beat too long before throwing a late pass intended for London on a shallow route. Walley read it perfectly to jump in front of the pass, then briefly juggled the interception before he secured it and raced down the far sideline for a pick-six. The Colts defense erupted as they chased him toward the end zone to embrace the signature moment of the two-hour practice. it’s Walley’s world. pic.twitter.com/PooS119FUf — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) August 19, 2026 Walley continues to show just how impactful he can be as a starter. He missed his entire rookie season after suffering a torn ACL during a joint-practice against the Baltimore Ravens last August. Fittingly enough, Walley is on track to make his NFL debut against that same team. The 23-year-old has already spent the bulk of training camp challenging himself by staying attached to the hip of slot receiver Josh Downs, then took another step Wednesday as the starting outside cornerback. The joint-practice at Droplight Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, Ind. was the lone football practice that featured two of the NFL’s top five running backs. The Falcons began their first-team work with a heavy dose of Bijan Robinson, who ripped off consecutive explosive runs before adding chunk gains as a pass catcher out of the backfield. Robinson showcased his elite combination of acceleration, agility, and vision as one of the league’s most dangerous weapons. When the first-team All-Pro tailback was able to reach the second level, the stampede in blue struggled to corral him. Colts rookie strong safety A.J. Haulcy figured it out quickly though and raced to meet Robinson in the backfield for a tackle for loss. Defensive linemen Arden Key and Grover Stewart later combined to make a defensive stop on a toss play for Robinson. Third-year edge rusher Laiatu Latu threatened to ruin Atlanta’s game plan without ever getting an opportunity to touch Tagovailoa. Latu’s burst was especially noticeable as he seemed to get into the backfield untouched on multiple plays, including one sequence in which Key also came screaming off the opposite edge for what would have been a violent combined sack. Tagovailoa finished 8-of-13 passing against Indy’s first-team defense, with the lone explosive play through the air to London over Walley. London followed with a slick one-handed grab on a drag route during 7-on-7s that caught more awes from the crowd. Despite focusing on the defense, quarterback Daniel Jones had an immaculate performance without most of his weapons. Jones completed all 15 of his passes in team drills, distributing the ball while avoiding any unforced turnovers. Perhaps it was his final throw that may have been his best as Jones found Downs on a 30-yard crosser over the middle, delivering the ball just before a massive hit was waiting for his slot receiver. The Colts host one final joint-practice with the Falcons at Grand Park on Thursday, starting at 3 p.m.

title: Can Colts fans wrap their arms around Daniel Jones?
summary: The only QB competition going on in Colts camp, is for the backup role. Our starting QB will be making north of 40 million dollars, this year and next, whether it is believed that is a good number or not. He doesn’t have to show anything in the preseason and anyone who has laid eyes […]
full_text: The only QB competition going on in Colts camp, is for the backup role. Our starting QB will be making north of 40 million dollars, this year and next, whether it is believed that is a good number or not. He doesn’t have to show anything in the preseason and anyone who has laid eyes on his practices, report that they can’t tell that he has had an injury. If you put him out there after his ankle/leg injury last year, you are putting him out there this year with what you have witnessed. Not much is disclosed about jersey sales, but I can say that he was not listed among the top 50 sold in the league. He may not even have been the top selling Colts #17 last year? Granted, a Rivers #17 might complete some collections or be a nice novelty, but everyone knew that it would be a five game run at best. I’m not saying that Colts fans should have been all in on DJ. Heck, they didn’t even know that he would be the starter until AR took an ill advised sack in preseason. Still, at some point, you would think that the jersey of the starting QB of a team sitting atop the standings and putting up points at a “historic” rate, would be in demand. It might well have been, had he been able to stay on the field and complete in what would have surely been a welcomed playoff appearance. I can understand the reluctance. After all, he would be a free agent at the end of the season. Again, no shaming from me for our fans, as I tend to purchase a jersey of a player I expect to be around a while. Full disclosure, the last one I bought was a Darius Leonard. Now we move into a new season and Jones returns from a serious injury. We had a touch and go off-season contract negotiation period, where we didn’t know if he would be signed or franchise tagged. Many thought that he got a better contract than he should be given, although I believe most fans wanted his return. It is true that he now is still only locked in as a Colt for two years (there is actually an out after this year), with some void years that do not guarantee his being a Colt past 2027. My question is, “Given the chasm that we have had at QB since Luck’s untimely retirement, when will you feel comfortable saying that you want him here for the next 8 – 10 years and maybe even wear #17 proudly?” I’m personally already there. I feel he is an easy guy to root for. I see him as a grounded guy that his teammates embrace as their leader. He made some throws last year that were above “league average” throws. He no doubt benefitted from a scheme that played to his strengths, but he also made his pre and post snap reads that gave the play the best chance to work. Given the normal timeline for an achilles return, he had to have taken his rehab very seriously. Cool nicknames like, Danny Dimes, Indiana Jones, or just DJ are positives. Lastly, I saw what I saw last year and I liked it. I’m pretty sure that the most common response will be, “Let me see him do it for a whole year, before I embrace him.” and I guess that’s fair, but him becoming that guy would check a lot of positive boxes moving forward. I imagine that there may be a few holding out hope for AR or even Leonard and there are some that I think would rather be right than happy, so they want the money paid to DJ to represent another Ballard failure and be the one that finally gets him fired. It may not be a big deal? We didn’t buy Brissett, Rivers, Wentz, Ryan, Minshew, or Flacco jerseys and oddly enough more Richardson jerseys may have been purchased than any of them. After all, as the 4th pick, he did represent the future. So what would it take for you to embrace Daniel Jones as the future?
