title: 10 Observations from the Jaguars-Panthers Joint Practice
summary: Day 15 of Jacksonville Jaguars Training Camp brought the Carolina Panthers to the Miller Electric Center for Jacksonville’s second set of 2026 joint practices, and it brought the heat in more ways than one. A hot, physical Wednesday produced multiple altercations, genuine moments of dominance on both sides of the ball, and a roster move […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - JUNE 10: Defensive End Josh Hines-Allen #41 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during Mandatory Veteran Minicamp at Miller Electric Center on June 10, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images Day 15 of Jacksonville Jaguars Training Camp brought the Carolina Panthers to the Miller Electric Center for Jacksonville’s second set of 2026 joint practices, and it brought the heat in more ways than one. A hot, physical Wednesday produced multiple altercations, genuine moments of dominance on both sides of the ball, and a roster move that underscored just how significant the Jaguars’ offensive line injury situation has become. Here is a complete breakdown of the day. 1. Coen Undecided on Friday Starters Coen declined to commit to a definitive answer on which starters will play in Friday’s preseason opener. He indicated he wants to review the health status of the roster coming out of Wednesday’s practice and evaluate the tape before making a final determination in the next 24-hours. Based on the joint practice performance, I wouldn’t be shocked to see key starters rested. However, the team could opt to play isolated starters in need of an additional look. 2. Tempers Flare Early Joint practices have a well-earned reputation for physical intensity and Wednesday’s session delivered exactly that. Multiple skirmishes broke out throughout the day, beginning on the very first play of the live scrimmage period. A second altercation erupted after wide receiver Tim Jones absorbed a hard hit from Panthers safety Trayvon Moerig on an incompletion, with receiver Austin Trammell stepping in immediately afterward. The temperature, both literal and figurative, was a factor for the entire session. These are players who have spent two weeks going against the same teammates, and the energy that comes with a new opponent was evident from the opening snap. 3. Defense Sets The Tone Jacksonville’s defense arrived ready to make a statement, and the Carolina offense absorbed some significant collisions throughout the first half of practice. Antonio Johnson delivered a punishing hit on Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble, getting the defensive sideline going. Jalen Huskey leveled a separate Panthers’ tight end along the sideline in red zone period. Foye Oluokun put a big hit on running back Jonathan Brooks. This was all before the middle of practice. The defense set the tone early and often, and the Panthers, to their credit, simply got back in their huddle and kept competing. But the general read on the day: Jacksonville controlled the first half of practice decisively before the Panthers somewhat steadied themselves and made things slightly competitive after the break. 4. Red Zone O Nearly Perfect If there was a singular takeaway from the offensive side of the ball, it was the red zone. Lawrence and the Jacksonville offense were dominant in red zone periods, converting on nearly every attempt across eight to nine opportunities (lost count as I was on the opposite field). Nate Boerkircher, Tanner Koziol, Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr, CJ Williams, and others scored in the period, with a flurry of touchdown production. CJ Williams… @Dream_Finders | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/6vACTthkTv — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) August 19, 2026 5. Tuten’s Great Day This was easily the Tuten performance Jaguars fans have been waiting to see. He logged two clear long runs on the day, and by most accounts, it was his most complete individual practice of the entire training camp. Tuten just had maybe the best run I’ve seen from him in a Jaguars practice setting. A super smooth jump cut had the crowd oohing and aahing — Gus Logue (@gus_logue) August 19, 2026 When discussing the run game, Coen acknowledged the offensive line’s performance in his post-practice comments, a notable development given how much conversation the unit’s continuity and injury depth have generated in recent weeks. 6. Huge Day at Tight End Both Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol scored touchdowns in team periods and each had multiple physical runs after the catch, giving the Jaguars’ expanded tight end room a tangible showcase moment against a legitimate NFL defense. On the other side of that equation, Panthers linebacker Devin Lloyd, playing his first joint practice against his former team, gave up several catches in coverage, including one to Brenton Strange. The 2025 Jaguars defense that benefited enormously from Lloyd’s production had a front-row seat to watch him operate from the opposing sideline, with a very quiet day. He'll take that! @Dream_Finders | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/lEfkdADyPy — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) August 19, 2026 7. Pass Rush Heats Up As a note, I arrived to the pass rush one-on-one period a few minutes after they began. In my presence, the individual pass rush drills produced a range of results. Travon Walker went 3-1, opening with a strong bull rush and following it with a competitive rep that was difficult to definitively score, likely a pressure on the quarterback if graded in a game context. Davon Hamilton went 1-1 on the interior and added a Bryce Young sack in team periods. B.J. Green went 1-1 with a sharp outside speed rush rep and collected a sack in team periods along with at least one additional rep that would have graded as a pressure. Josh Hines-Allen went 0-2 in one-on-one drills, both times getting ridden around the pocket. Who won these one-on-one’s? #DUUUVAL #Keeppounding pic.twitter.com/cGRzvq795L — Action Sports Jax (@ActionSportsJax) August 19, 2026 But the one-on-one results were quickly rendered irrelevant once live action began. In team periods, Hines-Allen had no fewer than three would-be sacks, by my count. The full defensive front recorded between six and ten sacks, depending on the source, a level of production that reinforces the unit’s ceiling when healthy and engaged. BJ Green had two sacks, Dennis Gardeck had one (in the two-minute drill), Davon Hamilton had one, and there were multiple others that were at worst close pressures. It was a dominant day up front for Jacksonville’s defense by any measure. 8. Coen Emphasizes Turnovers Travis Hunter had the closest thing to a defensive turnover on the day, undercutting a deep out route from Panthers receiver David Moore and nearly pulling in what would have been an interception before the ball fell incomplete. It was a plus rep in coverage despite the incompletion. Notably, Hunter played just two snaps on offense on Wednesday. Coen addressed the defense’s turnover production specifically in his post-practice availability, noting that forcing turnovers, the unit’s signature trait in 2025, when they produced a franchise-record 31, remains a major point of emphasis. The caveat worth adding is that the front’s sack production Wednesday suggests the pressure is clearly there. Converting that pressure into takeaways when the contact is live is the next step. 9. Cameron Keeps Chopping Wood? With Parker Washington out this week due to an undisclosed injury, rookie receiver Josh Cameron took Wednesday to make a compelling case for himself heading into the preseason. One of the day’s best highlights was a deep-ball touchdown to Josh Cameron from Trevor Lawrence, a clean throw against tight coverage. Cameron, who has been among the most consistent rookie performers since the first padded practice, continues to shine when given opportunities. 10. The Faalele Trade The biggest news of the day arrived just before practice. The Jacksonville Jaguars acquired offensive lineman Daniel Faalele from the New York Giants in exchange for a reported 2027 sixth-round draft pick. Faalele, 26, is a 6-foot-8, 380-pound guard who was a fourth-round pick out of Minnesota in the 2022 NFL Draft and spent his first four NFL seasons with the Baltimore Ravens, with 34 consecutive starts. Gus Logue covered the trade here. Daniel Faalele signed a Veteran Salary Benefit contract with the Giants, therefore…

title: Report: Jaguars trade Day 3 pick for Giants OL Daniel Faalele
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have bolstered their depth along the offensive line by trading a late 2027 draft pick for New York Giants guard Daniel Faalele. The deal was first reported by Evan Barnes of Newsday Sports. It’ll be a 2027 sixth-rounder going to New York, per Ryan O’Halloran of The Florida Times-Union. Jacksonville had a […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - AUGUST 15: Daniel Faalele #77 of the New York Giants prior to the pre-season game against the Minnesota Vikings on August 15, 2026 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars have bolstered their depth along the offensive line by trading a late 2027 draft pick for New York Giants guard Daniel Faalele. The deal was first reported by Evan Barnes of Newsday Sports. It’ll be a 2027 sixth-rounder going to New York, per Ryan O’Halloran of The Florida Times-Union. Jacksonville had a need at the position following several offseason injuries. Patrick Mekari was expected to keep his starting job at right guard, but he’s now in danger of missing the season opener (if not more time) after recently undergoing back surgery . Cole Van Lanen is another projected starter with a murky recovery timeline; he’s currently on the PUP list as he works his way back from a knee injury sustained late last season. Walker Little, Chuma Edoga, and Emmanuel Pregnon have also missed time during training camp. “We came into camp with 16 (offensive linemen) and got down to about nine the other day,” head coach Liam Coen said after Wednesday’s joint practice with the Carolina Panthers. “When you have some of those things occur, you want to continue to find guys that have done it, guys that have played in this league at a high level. [Faalele has] some big size, and I’m looking forward to getting to know him. But the experience is really what matters.” Faalele was drafted by the Baltimore Ravens in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft. The Minnesota product started 1 game in his first two seasons, primarily serving as a backup swing tackle, before starting all 34 regular season games in the past two years at right guard. He earned PFF grades of 60.5 in 2024 (52nd among 83 guards) and 56.7 in 2025 (58th among 87 guards). After the Giants hired former Ravens head coach John Harbaugh, Faalele followed him to New York in free agency. He signed a one-year contract worth $1.402 million (Jacksonville will inherit a base salary of $1.215 million). Faalele was originally in line to start across from Jon Runyan, but then the Giants used the No. 10 pick they received in the Dexter Lawrence trade to draft Francis Mauigoa. According to The Athletic , “Faalele was locked into the second-team offensive line for the first two weeks of training camp before the Giants bumped up rookie left tackle JC Davis to the second team. That shifted Marcus Mbow to second-team right tackle and slid Josh Ezeudu from tackle to guard. Faalele also ceded some second-team reps to Evan Neal in recent practices.” As of today, I would guesstimate that Jacksonville’s 2026 Week 1 starting lineup will include Anton Harrison, Ezra Cleveland, Robert Hainsey, Van Lanen, and Little. One would assume that recent draft selections Pregnon, Wyatt Milum, and Jonah Monheim will also make the 53-man roster. It’ll be interesting to see who else the Jaguars keep between Mekari, Faalele, and Edoga. Jags fans, let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

title: Jaguars roster 2026: Montaric Brown, Chris Rodriguez, and Tanner Koziol are underrated
summary: In his first season as the Jacksonville Jaguars’ head coach, Liam Coen’s team went 13-4. The 2025 Jaguars rose from 26th in DVOA to sixth, from 26th to sixth in points scored, and from 27th to eighth in points allowed. It was a remarkable turnaround from 2024’s 4-13 record, and you could understand why Coen […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 6: Montaric Brown #1 of the Jacksonville Jaguars practices during training camp at Miller Electric Center on August 6, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images In his first season as the Jacksonville Jaguars’ head coach, Liam Coen’s team went 13-4. The 2025 Jaguars rose from 26th in DVOA to sixth , from 26th to sixth in points scored, and from 27th to eighth in points allowed. It was a remarkable turnaround from 2024’s 4-13 record, and you could understand why Coen was a bit unhappy that Jacksonville’s accomplishments went under the radar. After all, the New England Patriots went from 4-13 to 14-3 in 2025 — the other big swing last season — and they got most of the credit they deserved for that from national media. Of course, the Patriots also represented the AFC in Super Bowl LX, and the Jags were booted out of the playoffs in the Wild Card Round by the Buffalo Bills in an agonizingly close 27-24 game that was decided by Josh Allen’s 1-yard touchdown run with 1:04 left. Now coming into Season 2, Coen isn’t putting up with the alleged disrespect. “ You don’t have to make up the fire,” Coen said during a July appearance on 1010 XL in Jacksonville . “You don’t have to make it up. It’s given to us every day. It’s a gift from the heavens. I just go pull out of my phone, look up the NFL Network website and just pop it up here and I’m curious if I see any photos, or anything, about the Jacksonville Jaguars. I think I’ll just scroll right on through. “I think I’ll see 40 pictures of [Chicago Bears quarterback] Caleb Williams, and I won’t see a single thing about any of the players [from] here. So it’s beautiful. I’m going to tell these guys [his players] how much you all think they suck, and we’ll keep going.” Coen is far from the first coach to try and stir the pot to motivate his team, but does he have a point? Is America sleeping on the Jacksonville Jaguars? FTN (formerly Football Outsiders) projects the 2026 Jaguars with 8.9 average wins , a 49.3% chance to make the playoffs, a 5.5% chance to reach the Super Bowl, and a 2.4% chance to win it. The Houston Texans (11.3 average wins) and the Indianapolis Colts (9.1 average wins) are ahead of the Jags in the AFC South projections. I worked with Football Outsiders for years, so I know the huge amount of smart work Aaron Schatz and his crew put into what they do, but I can also imagine that those numbers feed into any inferiority complexes that might be out there. Of course, the best way to end all of this is to ( Jake Taylor voice ) win the whole bleeping thing. And for the 2026 Jaguars to win the whole bleeping thing, they’ll need the level best from everybody on the roster — not just the obvious names, but also the guys whose names aren’t as commonly known in a national sense. To that end, I’ve identified three Hidden Gems for the 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars — one underrated veteran, one underrated free agent signing, and one underrated draft pick. Underrated veteran: CB Montaric Brown The Jaguars selected Arkansas cornerback Montaric Brown with the 223rd overall pick in the seventh round of the 2022 draft, so it’s not as if much was expected. But Brown did what all later-round guys are supposed to do — he bided his time and made the most of every available opportunity. Brown’s snaps increased every season, and by 2024, coaches were talking about this “Buster” Brown guy, and how he was climbing up the charts. Last season, with 795 overall snaps and 539 in coverage, Brown allowed just 37 catches on 69 targets for 383 yards, 89 yards after the catch, three touchdowns, two interceptions, 10 pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 73.3 — by far his best to date. Brown really caught his new head coach’s attention in the Jags’ 30-29 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Injuries had depleted the cornerback room, and Brown had to step up — which he did. “Yeah, his feel for zone coverage has always been something that we’ve appreciated,” Coen said of Brown the day after that game. “We probably went into the game wanting to play a little bit more match/man to try to get on them and help our pass rush, but then obviously losing Travis and then J-Lew [CB Jourdan Lewis] may have put our guys in some tough spots in some of the man coverage, and it may be not what we’re best at the moment in some instances. ‘Buster’ has got great vision and anticipation. So just need to continue to find positive ways of putting these guys in positions to be successful down in and down out.” . @Jaguars CB Montaric Brown has improved in each of his four NFL seasons. Could 2026 see a new level of breakout? Love how he's learned to establish optimal position late in the down on deeper routes. pic.twitter.com/i7S0xA1TGX — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 11, 2026 And now, a 2026 cornerback group that has Brown and Hunter outside, and Lewis in the slot, could be a real strength. Underrated free agent: RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. Losing Travis Etienne to the New Orleans Saints after four productive seasons was a bit of a hit to Coen’s offense, but Coen had a blast from his past in mind to accentuate his running game. The Jags signed former Washington Commanders running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. to a two-year, $10 million contract with $6.2 million guaranteed. Rodriguez’s ties to Coen are clear — when Coen was Kentucky’s offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach in 2021, Rodriguez had his best collegiate season, running 224 times for 1,377 yards and nine touchdowns, adding 56 forced missed tackles and 18 runs of 15 or more yards to the mix. Rodriguez’s imprint hasn’t been quite as compelling in the NFL but last season for the Commanders in a shared backfield, he ran 112 times for 500 yards and five touchdowns. His 23 forced missed tackles and four runs of 15 or more yards speak to the two-headed profile of surprising speed and unsurprising power for a 6’0”, 224-pound back. Now, the three-year veteran will share the backfield with Bhayshul Tuten. New @Jaguars RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. In a word, BOOM. pic.twitter.com/2NguV8CDiG — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 11, 2026 “I think there’s a lot to like,” GM James Gladstone said in March, after Rodriguez agreed to terms. “Obviously, Liam has some familiarity with him dating back to his time at Kentucky. Beyond that, it’s kind of fun. If I unravel, sort of diving into who he’s been as a professional football player and get into the nuances of our exposure to him and the lead-up to the decision to prioritize him as an untendered RFA [restricted free agent]. “When we watch players, [Executive Vice President of Football Operations] Tony Boselli has been a consistent presence in that, but he’s fallen into the line of ‘If you watch the tape’ right before sharing his perspective on each player. We’ve kind of fallen into that becoming a funny comment, knowing that he’s usually talking to a group of people that have watched the tape. And so with that, Chris Rodriguez is in fact somebody that if you watch the tape, you understand very quickly exactly who he is as a football player, the superpowers that he taps into consistently. If you draw back to his time at Kentucky, it’s remained a constant. “He is very physical at the point of attack. He has a really good pace in his approach to the line of scrimmage and finding the lanes. Obviously, an intimate understanding of the system and how Liam likes to call things. So, there’s a lot of strong matches just generally from how those two in tandem can really work together. And then also our interest in continuing to find ways to level up our capacity in the run game to make it a really balanced attack, being able to attack the perimeter, and also the inside in really fair and balanced forms. I think that Chris seamlessly provides that.” He does, and don’t be surprised if Coen’s familiarity with what Rodriguez can do has him giving Rodriguez more and more opportunities. Whether you…

title: Steve Spagnuolo anxious to see what the Chiefs have in Mansoor Delane
summary: We are nearly done with Kansas City Chiefs training camp after three weeks up in St. Joe at Missouri Western State University. The final practice will be on Thursday, August 20th, ahead of the second preseason game of the season, on the road against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Saturday at 6:30 p.m. Arrowhead time. […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Cornerback Mansoor Delane #5 of the Kansas City Chiefs sits on the team bench during the fourth quarter of an NFL preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are nearly done with Kansas City Chiefs training camp after three weeks up in St. Joe at Missouri Western State University. The final practice will be on Thursday, August 20th, ahead of the second preseason game of the season, on the road against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Saturday at 6:30 p.m. Arrowhead time. Through the first preseason game, the team hasn’t seen much of No. 6 overall pick, cornerback Mansoor Delane. He donned a yellow, non-contact jersey for the majority of practices leading up to last weekend’s exhibition against the Los Angeles Rams. However, this week, he has been participating completely in camp practices. Defensive backs coach Dave Merritt described what he has seen from Delane now that he can play at full speed with full contact. “Seeing some of the things that we saw on tape coming out of LSU,” Merritt told local media after Wednesday’s practice. “He’s a guy who has sticky coverage, and getting him back in pads and seeing that you can actually tackle people now.” “Hopefully, that’s going to show up this weekend,” Merritt said, alluding to Delane possibly taking the field and playing live snaps for the first time this preseason. It would be a welcome update, one that defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has likely been waiting for. Earlier in camp, he admitted that there would be “a lot” for Delane to work on before Week 1 once he shed the non-contact label. Now, Spagnuolo can really coach up the crowned jewel of this year’s draft class. He shared an example of that with local media after Wednesday’s practice. “He’s definitely a competitor. We saw that on tape when we evaluated him,” Spagnuolo said about Delane. “But like a lot of these young guys… sometimes you’ve got to knock some practice habits out of them. I think Mansoor is learning that. I think he’s embracing it. I think the vets are pushing him toward that. It’s unfortunate that he’s missed all the time he’s missed, but we’ll try to get him caught up here.“ While Merritt was hopeful to see Delane playing on Saturday, Spagnuolo is really looking forward to the chance, but defers to head coach Andy Reid for the final say. “I don’t know what will happen with the game. That’ll be on Coach Reid,” Spags said. “But I’m anxious to get him out there and see what we’ve got.”

In coordination with the acquisition of Jones, the Chiefs waived defensive end Anthony Dunn. […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 21: Cam Jones #44 of the Kansas City Chiefs rushes the passer during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 21, 2024 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Wednesday morning, the Kansas City Chiefs announced that reserve linebacker Cam Jones has re-signed after more than a year away from the club, spending the 2025 season with the New York Jets and this offseason with the New York Giants . We have signed Free Agent LB Cam Jones. We have waived DE Anthony Dunn. pic.twitter.com/S4RZUVEqpL — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) August 19, 2026 In coordination with the acquisition of Jones, the Chiefs waived defensive end Anthony Dunn. The rookie, an undrafted defender from Toledo, was wearing No. 94 this preseason. The signing of veteran defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah may have contributed to Dunn being the odd man out for Jones. Cam Jones played in 38 games over the 2023 and 2024 seasons in Kansas City, mainly contributing on special teams. In 2024, he finished the regular season with the fourth-most special teams snaps on the team. Between the regular season and postseason, Jones logged 38 tackles and one quarterback hit during his stint with the Chiefs. Last season, he appeared in 10 games with the Jets and tallied five tackles. Jones will join a hampered linebacker room in Kansas City. Veteran Drue Tranquill is currently dealing with back spasms that have kept him out of practice; second-year linebacker Jeffrey Bassa recovered quickly from a groin injury and played well in the preseason opener, but the departure of linebacker Leo Chenal this offseason leaves the position thinner than usual. New(ish) Chiefs LB Cam Jones is wearing No. 45 in his second stint with the team. Formerly wore 44 from 2023-24 with the club. Chiefs waived DE Anthony Dunn to make room for Jones. — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) August 19, 2026 Jones is wearing No. 45 with the Chiefs, according to Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com .

title: Examining the Chiefs’ rookie defensive linemen in Preseason Week 1
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs lost their preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams 20-12 on Saturday, in a game where minimal starters participated. The final score was far from the most important thing that happened throughout the day, and the Chiefs got a chance to look at multiple new players across the roster. Included in […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Defensive end R. Mason Thomas #51 of the Kansas City Chiefs rushes to the quarterback in the second quarter during an NFL preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost their preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams 20-12 on Saturday, in a game where minimal starters participated. The final score was far from the most important thing that happened throughout the day, and the Chiefs got a chance to look at multiple new players across the roster. Included in this group were Kansas City’s two rookie defensive linemen, Peter Woods and R Mason Thomas. Both players were top-50 picks in the NFL Draft back in April, and so far through camp, both have drawn headlines with solid play and shown flashes of becoming quality NFL starters. Preseason results don’t matter, but individual performances can show where a player is in their development and where they need to improve. Peter Woods After becoming the talk of camp with multiple terrific players and flashing high-level athletic ability, Woods was fairly quiet during his professional debut. That’s not to say he played badly, but we didn’t quite see the explosive, penetrating ability he showed through most of training camp. The Rams’ offense ran multiple rollout passes and plays that moved the pocket, preventing the Chiefs defensive line from getting too many rushes off, which can make it hard for defensive tackles to get going. Woods still managed to show a few flashes of his talent, even if he didn’t show up in the box score. Wood best pass rush snap of the day. Had trouble getting going with all the rollout looks and quick hitters, but this shows the kind of penetrator and disruptor he can be just by being quick off the snap. I like the bend he showed to redirect and chase the QB. pic.twitter.com/0s4oK30rPI — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 18, 2026 On the snap, the Rams sell a run, but the quarterback quickly pulls the ball and rolls out to the opposite side of the field. Woods, lined up as the 3-technique, quickly works to beat the tackle across his face in the B gap to defend against the run. When the quarterback pulls the ball, Woods quickly redirects himself and works to get free of the down blocking tackle to pursue the quarterback. This play may not be the most memorable, but it shows where Woods will make an impact as a rookie. His ability to quickly penetrate in both the run and pass game in one-on-one situations will be where he makes plays. The burst off the ball was good, and had it actually been a run, he would have had a good shot at making the stop. Woods was double-teamed multiple times during traditional pocket passing plays, but without those double teams, he likely would have created more pressure. Woods delivers alot of power off the snap. If not for the cente stepping over to help out could have been quick pressure. Like the effort to finish the snap. pic.twitter.com/O3euHZ6kj8 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 18, 2026 On the snap, Woods puts a big jolt into the right guard with a bull rush, visibly knocking him back, and if not for the center coming over to assist, this could have turned into a nice rush for Woods. When the center does come over to assist, Woods transitions out of power and works to get around the guard. The ball is out of the quarterback’s hands quickly, but Woods still showed a good effort in recovering from the double team and worked to bend his way around the guard to pressure the quarterback. There are plenty of things Woods can improve on from his first professional outing, but all in all, Chiefs fans should still be excited about his game and how he will be able to impact games when out there with the Chiefs’ full defensive line. R Mason Thomas It would be hard to find a player who flashed more on Saturday than Thomas. Although Woods has garnered most of the headlines from training camp, Thomas started to come on strong during week two in St.Joe. In the game, he showed off his quick burst off the ball on more than one occasion. Thomas, lightning-quick, steps in quickly, gets into the tackle, lands inside the hands, and then slips the block late to put pressure on the QB. pic.twitter.com/0dqaaPFLlZ — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 17, 2026 On a critical third down in the low red zone, Thomas came blazing off the snap, quickly landed inside with hands on the left tackle, and managed to slip past using low pad level. The pressure forces a quick throw into coverage and an incompletion. Leaving Oklahoma, many labeled Thomas a pass-rush specialist, but in camp and this past weekend he has done a good job showing he can make plays in the run game. Thomas is doing a good job of fighting through the block and coming up with the tackle. pic.twitter.com/TsBQs0QuMd — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 17, 2026 On the snap, Thomas reads the tight end’s block and the running back’s path, and does a good job of shooting his hands through the tight end’s chest, delivering contact and knocking him back. When the back makes his read, Thomas quickly disengages from the block and helps make the stop. While his overall game was nice, there was one snap from Thomas at the end of the first half that should have everyone excited. Thomas is even a little slow off the snap, but the recovery and close-down time on the QB is something the team has not had in a while. pic.twitter.com/GTBqvh70tG — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 18, 2026 On the final play of the first half, Thomas lines up out wide and goes to work on the right tackle. Even after being a bit late off the snap, he accelerates quickly and bends the arc with no trouble. The quarterback tries to roll out to buy more time, but Thomas is rolling fast around the corner and forces him to throw the ball away. Getting off the field on critical snaps in the NFL is critical, and it seems that Thomas will be poised to play on plenty this season. The bottom line The first week of the preseason gave both of the Chiefs’ rookie defensive linemen a good chance to get their feet wet in a live-action scenario. For Woods, the slow day hardly represents the flash he has shown in practice so far, and as he takes more snaps— and more snaps with other starters— he should start to find his stride rushing the passer and creating plays in the backfield. Thomas flashed with his burst off the edge, but now he must show that he can do it consistently, and against a higher level of competition every week. Overall, this duo is still on pace to each play considerable snaps this season, and will be worth keeping an eye on in preseason Week 2.

title: Chiefs Mailbag: Why did Chris Jones and Kenneth Walker dress Saturday?
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! Some individual players shined in the preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams, but the players who took the field largely underwhelmed in the loss. Let’s see what’s on […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Defensive tackle Chris Jones #95 of the Kansas City Chiefs waves to fans during the fourth quarter of an NFL preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! Some individual players shined in the preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams , but the players who took the field largely underwhelmed in the loss. Let’s see what’s on readers’ minds ahead of this week’s preseason contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . saintschiefsfan asks: Why did running back Kenneth Walker dress and not get a single carry? What was the point of defensive tackle Chris Jones playing one snap? Was that head coach Andy Reid’s ”punishment” for him saying he doesn’t want to play in preseason ? My impression is that head coach Andy Reid has moved on from some anachronistic tendencies with starters in the preseason. We used to be able to predict like clockwork when certain players would enter and exit exhibitions. That has not been the case for the last couple of preseason slates. Perhaps Reid is seeing diminishing value in what you actually see during the game with known players. However, I also think Reid values seeing how the team operates pregame. While the Rams reportedly left most of their noteworthy players at home in Los Angeles, the Chiefs had all nominally available players fully dressed on the sideline. The team went through normal pregame workouts. Rather than getting any look at what Walker can do with the ball in his hands, I think the coaches wanted to see him in the huddle for the first play. Reid was likely assessing his team’s readiness to start a game. That said, there is probably an alternate universe where Jones keeps his mouth shut and gets the same treatment as veteran tight end Travis Kelce. Other than newly signed defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah, Kelce was the only player completely scratched on Saturday who wasn’t known to be recovering from a recent injury. Andyreidsmustache_ asks: Did we find at least one answer to our WR problem that’s plagued us since Tyreek Hill left in rookie Cyrus Allen? Allen certainly passed the first test. Two weeks after escaping an injury scare with only a shin bruise, Allen made the starting lineup and was on the field for over half of the offensive snaps. Climbing the ladder to bring in a high pass from quarterback Garrett Nussmeier was easily one of the plays of the game. Encouragingly, Allen was used strictly on offense, with no special teams snaps. An earlier exit in the next two contests would be an even bigger step forward. There is little value in seeing Allen’s route running against opponents’ deep depth players. We need to see as much action as possible against players who will at least be on 53-man rosters this season. There’s definitely a chance Allen ends 2026 and enters next season as one of the Chiefs’ starting wideouts. He has done everything the right way so far and looks much more game-ready than previous young wideouts we have seen linger on Kansas City’s bench. The same wild cards for any young player, however, are still in front of Allen. Namely, health (often via pure dumb luck) is the biggest variable that determines how a player’s career unfolds. If Allen starts seeing the field early, we will also need to wait until opposing defensive staffs have ample game film on him to see what adjustments he can make. LocoMotorKate asks: When will we get an adequate run defense? Hopefully, once the players who will actually be charged with run defense are on the field? It was not a great showing, to be fair. But some of the players who saw heavy snap counts may not even be good candidates for the Chiefs’ practice squad (and probably saw some of their chances plummet even further). Starting base defensive end Ashton Gillotte and weakside linebacker Drue Tranquill did not play due to injury. Jones played only the first snap, and middle linebacker Nick Bolton and defensive end George Karlaftis left after three plays. Nose tackle Khyiris Tonga — who will be on the field for obvious run downs — played only five snaps. The 1797 rushing yards Kansas City allowed in 2025 ranked ninth best in the league. That number is probably actually negatively skewed by the 410 yards allowed on the ground in the final three games after the season was lost. Given the returning players who have been dependable against the run with what should be a major upgrade inside with Tonga, I don’t think adequate run defense should rank high on concerns about the Chiefs, no matter how the bottom third of the 90-man roster played in 100-degree heat Saturday. If I were Brett Veach, however, I might scout linebackers and one-tech defensive tackles who could be on the roster bubble at other teams. The Chiefs should want to upgrade from some current deep depth options when building their practice squad (or even the bottom of the 53-man). kiddrsteve asks: Being that we play the Rams in regular season, do you feel Andy held back on the play calling. Most play calling very basic. Why kick a FG down 11 with 2 minutes left? Appears he held back going for the TD as he may show something. I don’t think Butker needs practice on extra point FGs To be fair, Butker missed four extra points in 2025. Missing on what should be the most anticlimactic play in sports also sometimes feels like a precursor to a more serious slump. So, I would definitely like to see him get some extra point tries. Saturday’s game definitely felt like Reid and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo had certain plays and formations they wanted to see no matter what the Rams were showing on the field. The players on the field trying to keep their football dreams alive assuredly would love an aggressive game plan. In reality, they are often helping the coaches evaluate formations they plan to eventually use with the more talented players on the bench. Spagnuolo will almost never blitz in the preseason, and this is likely doubly true for opponents he will see again. For his part, Reid seems to have more of a going-through-the-motions approach to the preseason than he used to, although I genuinely believe he wanted a strong sample from Allen, Nussmeier, and rookie running back Emmett Johnson. My favorite criticism I have seen online is that the Chiefs were lazy on the onside kick attempt with two minutes remaining. I do not have faith that the special teams staff has a revolutionary idea in the back of their minds for onside kicks. But if they did, preseason would be a terrible time to try it out. 5crawfishdinners asks: With Nussmeier looking as good as he did, would the Chiefs feel comfortable trading quarterback Justin Fields if a team offered something significant. Nussmeier should be passed over current No. 2 quarterback Fields on the depth chart is easily the most frequent hot take after Saturday. It’s not going to happen. Nussmeier played well, but let’s not overreact to one preseason game. There is value in having a backup quarterback who has at least been in NFL meeting rooms and led a professional huddle. The truth is, I don’t think either Fields or Nussmeier is going to keep Kansas City’s season afloat if needed for a multi-game stretch. Could Nussmeier eventually settle in as a Matt Moore or Chad Henne tier of backup? That’s certainly possible, but it would be silly to count on that happening in 2026. I do expect the rookie to be given a chance to win the backup job outright a year from now. The chances of being offered something significant for Fields are unlikely. The Chiefs acquired him in March for only a 2027 sixth-round pick. If any team were interested, it’s not like Kansas City’s offer would have been prohibitively expensive to top. Fields is set for free agency…

title: Chiefs News: Former special teams coach Frank Gansz Jr. passes away
summary: The latest There was an unfortunate passing in Chiefs Kingdom over the weekend: former special teams coordinator and the son of former Kansas City Chiefs head coach Frank Gansz Sr. passed away at the age of 64. Thank you to friends of the site, Chief Concerns, for sharing the information with Arrowhead Pride so we […]
full_text: BIRMINGHAM, ALABAMA - MARCH 31: Tight Ends and Special Teams coach Frank Gansz Jr. of the Tampa Bay Bandits poses for his 2022 USFL headshot at Protective Stadium on March 31, 2022 in Birmingham, Alabama. (Photo by Fox Sports/USFL/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest There was an unfortunate passing in Chiefs Kingdom over the weekend: former special teams coordinator and the son of former Kansas City Chiefs head coach Frank Gansz Sr. passed away at the age of 64. Thank you to friends of the site, Chief Concerns , for sharing the information with Arrowhead Pride so we can remember a unique member of the team’s history. Frank Gansz Jr., former Chiefs coordinator & head coach’s son, has died | The Kansas City Star During the 2003 season, when the Chiefs won the AFC West with a 13-3 record, they led the league in both punt-return average (16.4) and kick-return average (25.4). Dante Hall led the NFL in punt-return average, punt-return touchdowns and kickoff-return touchdowns. The Chiefs also blocked two field-goal attempts that season. In the previous two seasons, the Chiefs blocked four punts. In 2003, Gary Stills made the Pro Bowl as a special-teams player, and Kendall Gammon went to the NFL’s all-star game the following season as a long-snapper. Five Observations from Tuesday’s Practice | Chiefs Training Camp 8/18 | The Mothership 3. Cornerback Mansoor Delane logged a pass-breakup on a quick slant during a 7-on-7 period. Delane, who fully participated in a padded practice for the first time at training camp on Monday, was back at it and making plays on Tuesday. Notably, Delane – the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft – recorded a pass-breakup on a quick slant during 7-on-7 drills. Elsewhere in the secondary, cornerback Melvin Smith also notched a pass-breakup on a quick throw over the middle during the same period. Chiefs $11 Million Wide Receiver Exits Practice on Cart With Injury Tuesday | Heavy Sports A report at about 11:10 am CT by ESPN’s Nate Taylor, citing information from the Chiefs, said that Thornton had suffered a “strained hamstring.” With the severity of the hamstring injury not immediately clear, the receiver’s sudden departure leaves the Chiefs awaiting an update that could have significant implications for their offense. That receiver is Tyquan Thornton, who spent time in the medical tent before walking under his own power to the cart, then rode off the practice field from the sideline, according to injury analyst Jeff Mueller, a physical therapist who tracks NFL camps. The specific nature of Thornton’s injury or its severity had not been officially confirmed as of early Tuesday afternoon. A former Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver just became a free agent, but Brett Veach might be better off avoiding a reunion | A to Z Sports Smith-Schuster was with K.C. again last year in 2025, notching 33 receptions for 345 yards and a single touchdown. The Chiefs let Smith-Schuster leave in free agency this offseason as they sought to rebuild their skill-position group and go in a different direction. Now that Smith-Schuster is available again, and the Chiefs are facing some injuries in the wide receiver room, it could be enticing for GM Brett Veach to bring back the veteran. He’d immediately be the most experienced receiver on the roster, having played in the NFL since 2017 when he entered the league out of USC with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Emari Demercado’s late preseason debut raises questions about Chiefs’ backfield plans | FanSided Entering the fourth quarter in the preseason is typically a sign that you’re unlikely to make the roster or a fringe depth piece that is going to need an epic run to stick around. As harsh as this might seem, it is the reality of the business and part of the next month, as a large number of players will see their careers end, be forced to seek out a new landing spot, or hope to earn a practice squad role. Demercado doesn’t seem to fit any of the above, based on Kansas City seeking him out in free agency and having a clear question mark when it comes to depth at the position. Kenneth Walker III is going to get the bulk of the carries; this much is clear. Around the NFL Chargers center Tyler Biadasz carted off practice field with apparent leg injury | The Athletic Those were the scenes Tuesday as the Los Angeles Chargers held a joint practice with the San Francisco 49ers at The Bolt. On the seventh rep of practice for the first-team offense, starting center Tyler Biadasz suffered an apparent left leg injury. Left guard Kayode Awosika threw a 49ers defensive lineman into the back of Biadasz’s leg. Biadasz went down immediately. Trainers came out and treated him for a couple of minutes. Biadasz was then helped onto a cart. He could not put any weight on his left leg. Multiple brawls mar Saints-Cowboys joint practice session | ESPN Punches were thrown, helmets were tossed, and at one point, Saints tight end Brock Rechsteiner, son of WWE Hall of Famer Scott Steiner, grabbed a Cowboys player and body-slammed him to the turf. That scuffle happened after Cowboys cornerback Caelen Carson punched Rechsteiner, who was then yanked around by the face mask as teammates poured in. The situation between the two teams was heated enough that Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer and Saints coach Kellen Moore discussed whether to continue. Commissioner Roger Goodell says ‘no doubt’ there eventually will be NFL team outside U.S. | NFL.com “At some point, there will be NFL teams outside the USA,” Goodell said, per ESPN.com. “I have no doubt that this will happen one day.” Goodell’s comments came during an appearance with German outlet RTL/ntv ahead of a record nine international games this season, including a Week 10 game in Munich between the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions. NFL owners in May passed a resolution to allow an increase to 10 international games beyond the 2026 season, and Goodell has stated in the past that the league’s goal is to play 16 international games. I had a lot of stiffness last year,” Wiley shared. “Still was dealing with some swelling and stuff like that. “I would say the main thing though is mentally – just mentally trust yourself,” Wiley continued. “Being able to do OTAs this offseason was a huge help. Just working through a bunch of that stuff and then by the time the season gets here you repeat these things so many times that you don’t even think about it anymore. Where last year, I felt like I was thinking about a lot before I was going in and out of breaks, before I was doing stuff.” From The Feed Follow Arrowhead Pride on Social Media Facebook: Like our page Instagram: @ArrowheadPride X: Follow @ArrowheadPride AP Staff on X: See complete list 90.9 The Bridge on X: Follow @909thebridge

summary: The Chargers are at home in SoFi Stadium on Thursday night to host the San Francisco 49ers in Preseason Week Two. full_text: EL SEGUNDO, CALIFORNIA - MAY 19: Charlie Kolar #88 of the Los Angeles Chargers catches the ball during offseason workout at The Bolt on May 19, 2026 in El Segundo, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers are at home in SoFi Stadium on Thursday night to host the San Francisco 49ers in Preseason Week Two. Their joint practice — outside of the deflating injury to center Tyler Biadasz — went rather well for the Chargers who reportedly diced up the Niners defense through most of the day. After hearing how well things were as far as what the Chargers could control on Tuesday, I have my hopes high for another entertaining preseason game. With that said, here are five Chargers I’m excited to watch when these two teams take the field Thursday night. TE Charlie Kolar Kolar is considered a starter and will likely only play one game, but that small sample size could still be our first look at how Mike McDaniel plans to use him in his offense. Despite being one of the best run-blocking tight ends in the NFL, Kolar has always had untapped receiving ability that was not often used in Baltimore with both Mark Andrews and Isaiah Likely playing on the same offense. But with the Chargers, you can fully expect McDaniel to find a way to utilize his 6’6, 265-pound pass-catcher. thoughts from Chargers camp: – LOTs of Charlie Kolar, TE versatility – Akheem Mesidor is story of camp – Unclear when Slater returns, LG wide open – Rookie Genesis Smith could play right away, 2 UDFA DBs could make team – McDaniel: personnel allows them to run everything — Gregg Rosenthal (@greggrosenthal) August 12, 2026 RB Omarion Hampton Another starter so we will only get one drive, but after seeing Hampton run through the face of multiple 49ers during their joint practice, I am only more hyped to see him back on the field, especially if he plans on doing that some more Thursday night. Hampton is one of many players we cannot wait to see in McDaniels’ offense, and that goes especially for him as the team’s RB1 in a system that should let him be at his most productive. Omarion Hampton trucked Ji'Ayir Brown 💀 Via: @JasonDelgado78 pic.twitter.com/2oVwnrYcbN — OurSF49ers (@OurSf49ers) August 18, 2026 CB Eric Rogers Rogers had a standout preseason as an undrafted rookie that included a two-interception game. He unfortunately wound up injured and placed on season-ending IR prior to final cuts, but the team saw all they needed to in that span to know they wanted to keep him around. The former Scarlet Knight out of Rutgers has had a quiet camp thus far for the Chargers, but he snatched an interception in the joint practice that was one of the highlights of the session. He’ll need to do that another time or two if he wants to stay in the race for a practice squad spot amongst a cornerback room with tons of potential around him. D.J. Uiagalelei After he outperformed Trey Lance against the Texas, I’m ready to see if he can put his stake further into the backup quarterback position with another strong outing against the Niners. Uiagalelei has been a consistent performer in practice (based on everything we keep hearing out of camp) and it sounds like he’s gotten a bit proficient with the deep ball. Compared to Lance who we often hear about throwing more interceptions than touchdowns during 11-on-11 drills. DJU should get just as many, if not, more snaps than he received in Houston and I can’t wait to see what he ends up doing with another opportunity. C Jacob Spomer Spomer was the highest-graded offensive player for the Chargers that played over 50 snaps against the Texans. His overall grade of 82.0 was otherwise second best on the team behind Kayode Awosika who played just 15 snaps. Spomer looked poised and under control while playing in his first professional game. He handled stunts well and blocked his tail off, earning the third-highest pass block (82.0) and run block grade (79.7) amongst all players. Out of nowhere, the Chargers all of a sudden like they may have a little diamond in the rough with Spomer. The former Fresno State Bulldog actually started at left tackle prior to the 2025 season and only played one year of center before signing with the Chargers. title: Undrafted free agent making a case for Chargers’ 53-man roster
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are figuring out how they are going to dwindle their roster from 90 players to 53 in the next couple of weeks. It’s not as easy as it sounds, especially when undrafted free agents like Nadame Tucker are playing higher than their expectations. Tucker led Division I last year with 14.5 […]
full_text: Feb 26, 2026; Indianapolis, IN, USA; Western Michigan defensive lineman Nadame Tucker (DL61) during the NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Los Angeles Chargers are figuring out how they are going to dwindle their roster from 90 players to 53 in the next couple of weeks. It’s not as easy as it sounds, especially when undrafted free agents like Nadame Tucker are playing higher than their expectations. Tucker led Division I last year with 14.5 sacks at Western Michigan, but he still went undrafted, which allowed the Chargers to sign him after the draft. Tucker continued to make a strong case for himself to play for the Chargers with one of the team’s two quarterback hits in the 27-7 win over the Houston Texans. “It feels like I belong,” Tucker said via the team’s website . “I know the type of guys I’m around, the stuff I can gain from them. I come with that approach like I belong here, I’m not starstruck in any way. I want to be just like those guys in a way. Just try to pay attention to every little detail.” Tucker still has a long way to go to make the 53-man roster, with players like Khalil Mack, Tuli Tuipulotu and first-round pick Ahkeem Mesidor standing in his way in a stacked outside linebacker group, but he is still going to keep pushing, as anything can happen in training camp and the preseason. “That’s my biggest thing, just knowing where I’m at as far as in the league and guys I’m going against and building off that,” Tucker said. “Even taking reps against Joe [Alt] and some of those guys, I’m trying to get in those as much as I can just to see where I’m at and build off that because I’m trying to be a Pro Bowler.” BFTB community, how do you feel about Tucker’s chances of making the roster? Could he sneak on as an additional pass rusher? Let us know in the comments section below.

title: Chargers C Tyler Biadasz out ‘indefinitely’ with ACL damage
summary: After initial screenings following Tuesday’s joint practice with the 49ers, Chargers center Tyler Biadasz was ruled to have damage to his ACL, on top of “additional injuries” to his left leg, per multiple reports. In a statement from the Chargers, Biadasz is “currently in the process of gathering additional opinions.” If there wasn’t a complete […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers center Tyler Biadasz (63) at training camp at The Bolt. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After initial screenings following Tuesday’s joint practice with the 49ers, Chargers center Tyler Biadasz was ruled to have damage to his ACL, on top of “additional injuries” to his left leg, per multiple reports. In a statement from the Chargers, Biadasz is “currently in the process of gathering additional opinions.” Chargers center Tyler Biadasz is out indefinitely after suffering damage to his ACL and additional injuries to his left knee during Tuesday’s joint practice against the 49ers, per @rapsheet and me. Biadasz will meet with more doctors to try to get more clarity. pic.twitter.com/0cyNFBmUdY — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 19, 2026 If there wasn’t a complete tear of the ACL, Biadasz may have dodged a major bullet, but this injury likely spells an extended period of time missed, if not still the entire 2026 season. Biadasz was signed to a three-year, $30 million contract early this offseason and he was only set to have a cap hit of $4.25 million in 2026 before that number jumps to $12.75 million in 2027. His dead cap hit in 2028, the final year of his deal, is only $3 million, meaning the Chargers have a built-in exit if needed without taking on a massive loss. For the time being, it looks like Jake Slaughter will be the team’s starting center moving forward with Kayode Awosika now the front-runner to start at left guard, although he will still likely battle a bit with Branson Taylor in the short-term. If Slaughter performs well as a rookie, it’d be interesting to see how the Chargers handle their interior heading into 2027. If Slaughter is the better player by then, $13 million is a lot of money to have sitting on the bench. Would the Chargers push Slaughter back to left guard? Would they look for a trade? A lot of questions and concerns are going to float around this situation over the next 12 months.
