title: How bright is the NY Giants’ future? ESPN isn’t very optimistic
summary: New York Giants fans are filled with optimism, feeling the future is brighter after more than a decade of struggle. The team has an accomplished head coach in John Harbaugh. There is a quarterback in place in Jaxson Dart who looks like he could be the answer at the position for the next decade. So, […]
full_text: New York Giants fans are filled with optimism, feeling the future is brighter after more than a decade of struggle. The team has an accomplished head coach in John Harbaugh. There is a quarterback in place in Jaxson Dart who looks like he could be the answer at the position for the next decade. So, Giants fans have plenty to be optimistic about. Right? ESPN analysts are not so sure. In its ‘ Future Power Rankings ’ covering the 2027-2029 seasons, ESPN ranks the Giants No. 22 in the 32-team NFL. ESPN uses four categories, and ranks the Giants as follows in those: Overall roster excluding QB — No. 29 Quarterback — No. 18 Coaching — No. 14 Front office — No. 32 ESPN says: Reason for hope: The Giants look like they might have a franchise quarterback in Jaxson Dart, and they certainly have a tenured and historically successful coach in John Harbaugh. It’s tough to rank a front office in questionable power under GM Joe Schoen, but emergent young stars such as Malik Nabers and Abdul Carter could give the Giants a strong bedrock for future growth. — Solak Reason for concern: As exciting as the upside is for Dart, Nabers and RB Cam Skattebo, their availability worries me. Nabers is coming off a significant knee injury, Skattebo is returning from a significant lower leg injury, and Dart has to modify his play style by reducing the number of hits he absorbs. — Riddick There is more bad news. ESPN has all three of the Giants’ NFC East competitors ranked above them. The Philadelphia Eagles are No. 2, Dallas Cowboys No. 16, and Washington Commanders No. 20. Valentine’s View Let me comment first on ESPN’s four bullet points: Overall roster — The Giants’ roster is far from complete. I believe, though, that there is enough talent that the Giants should be higher than that. Quarterback — Jaxson Dart still has much to prove. The Giants have to hope that he ends up outplaying the 18th spot. Coaching — Harbaugh at 14? Really? Front office — The worst front office in the league just got a draft pick in exchange for Daniel Faalele . If Dart becomes the quarterback the Giants think he will become, and the Giants can stop losing the impressive young talent they have begun collecting to major injuries, they will outplay the 22nd spot on the ESPN list. Of course, the rankings of the Eagles, Cowboys, and Commanders show that the yearly path through the NFC East is not going to be easy.

title: Cam Skattebo ‘felt great’ in first game action since gruesome injury
summary: The New York Giants may have lost to the Minnesota Vikings in their first preseason game, but there were still positives to be taken from the loss. One of the biggest positives was the play of running back Cam Skattebo. Not only did Skattebo start the game and have a nice day with 19 yards […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo runs with the ball | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants may have lost to the Minnesota Vikings in their first preseason game, but there were still positives to be taken from the loss. One of the biggest positives was the play of running back Cam Skattebo. Not only did Skattebo start the game and have a nice day with 19 yards on just four carries, but he looked like himself out there. Skattebo ran with the pinballing physicality with which he played as a rookie. That was great to see considering how ugly the ankle injury that ended his rookie season was. “I felt great,” Skattebo said after practice on Monday. “I made some minor errors in my details of what I was doing, but for the most part, I felt good having the ball in my hands.” “It was minor details, nothing serious,” he added. “Stuff I’ve just got to clean up in the film room, just little tiny things with my footwork on certain plays and stuff.” “Other than that, I felt good.” It certainly wasn’t a surprise to see Skattebo out on the field. As gruesome as his injury was, it was reported early on that the rehab would be relatively straight forward. In fact, the over-rotatedd backflip that had much of the media up in arms just before the start of camp showed that he was producing more force than he expected. But still, it was good to see Skattebo out on the field and looking good. There will obviously be aches and pains as he pushes himself to not just get back on the field, but be even better than he was as a rookie. “I think he [head coach John Harbaugh] knows that there’s more to me,” Skattebo said. “When I start pushing myself to get better and better each day, there are certain things that bother me here and there, but it’s not stuff that lingers around or hangs around. It’ll hop up on me here, and then it’ll go away tomorrow.” That’s typical of the rehab process, and even just of pushing yourself to improve progressively. The important part is recognizing the difference between “hurt” and “injured”, and being smart about knowing when to push and when to draw back. “Just working out those kinks and those bruises and stuff, and as time goes on, I’ll feel better and better.” The loss of Skattebo was a significant blow to the Giants a year ago, but his personality and burgeoning celebrity has overshadowed his recovery process. To be fair, Skattebo hasn’t exactly eschewed the limelight, though his sizeable personality also draws eyes in the New York fishbowl. “It’s New York. You get publicity,” Skattebo said. “What we say is all publicity is good publicity. If they’re talking about you, that’s a good thing. So, everyone loves to talk about me because I’m crazy and do a whole bunch of different things here and there. “That’s been my whole life, though. With my whole life, each level that I’ve went up, I think the football skills asset people think is less and less as we get higher and higher, and I think I only get better and better with the competition.” In many ways, Skattebo is the same guy off the field as on it. He’s already built a reputation as the loudest guy on the practice field, and is brash between the lines as well. There have been many analysts and commentators who’ve opined this summer that Skattebo’s playing style is going to limit his career. “People know I’m crazy, I like to run through people instead of run around them,” he said. “Hopefully you’ll see more running around people this year. I don’t really care what people think.” He isn’t going to be changing the running style that got him to this point. But, like teammate Jaxson Dart, Skattebo does recognize that he needs to be a bit smarter about when to run over opponents and when to pass on taking on contact. “I think Coach Harbs loves that I run right over the top of people,” Skattebo said. “Physicality is his number one thing, and it gets the o-line going even more. So, obviously, I mean, as I came back from injury and learning how to take less hits and try to maneuver better around people instead of through them and realizing that I could have got four more yards if I would have just took a step to the left. I think those are things that I’m just going to continue to add to my game and add to my bag of tools that I can pull from to make sure that I stay healthy and I stay successful.”

title: Eagles-Patriots Joint Training Camp Practice Notes: Day 1
summary: Today marked the thirteenth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. It was an action-packed joint training camp session against the New England Patriots. Here’s what I observed up at the New Balance Athletics Center in the shadow of Gillette Stadium from Foxboro, Massachusetts! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES UP NEXT: The Eagles […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 19: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots looks to catch a pass as he is defended by Quinyon Mitchell #27 of the Philadelphia Eagles during a joint practice at Gillette Stadium on August 19, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today marked the thirteenth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. It was an action-packed joint training camp session against the New England Patriots. Here’s what I observed up at the New Balance Athletics Center in the shadow of Gillette Stadium from Foxboro, Massachusetts! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES OVERALL PERFORMANCE: The Pats looked like the better team in the first of these two joint training camp practices. They started strong before the Eagles made up some ground … only for New England to pick it back up and finish on top. It wasn’t like the Birds got thoroughly dominated, though. EAGLES INJURY REPORT: DID NOT PARTICIPATE: DT Byron Young (shoulder) New injury. CB Jonathan Jones (shoulder) WR Johnny Wilson (knee) TE Grant Calcaterra (back) CB Jakorian Bennett (knee) OT John Ojukwu (pectoral) RB Dameon Pierce (hamstring) CB Shaun Wade (eye/shoulder) LIMITED PARTICIPATION: WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) Smitty did some work in position drills once again. WR Makai Lemon (hamstring) Lemon was upgraded to limited after previously being listed under DNP since early in camp. Positive sign. That being said, Lemon didn’t actually suit up and at least take part in position drills. He did do some post-practice running/cutting rehab work. Perhaps he returns to practice early next week following the Eagles’ second preseason game? EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby (ankle) CB Tariq Castro-Fields (heel) FULL PARTICIPATION RB Tank Bigsby, CB Mac McWilliams, S Cole Wisniewski, WR Danny Gray, and EDGE Jose Ramirez were removed from the injury report. IN-PRACTICE INJURIES: Dontayvion Wicks got banged up at one point but he returned shortly after. Fred Johnson was spotted leaving practice early with a trainer, according to Martin Frank . ACTIVE/PHYSICALLY UNABLE TO PERFORM EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) Prior to practice, Vic Fangio said the following: “I don’t know when Greenard will be back. That injury he got in our weight room is going to take some time to heal.” Fangio was also asked if he’s worried about Greenard missing the start of the season. His answer: “Yeah.” Not great! RESERVE/NON-FOOTBALL INJURY S Tucker Large Prior to practice, a pocket of Eagles green in a sea of Patriots fans got some fairly loud “E-A-G-L-E-S, EAGLES!” chants going. I also thought the Eagles fans in attendance cheering for their favorite team’s arrival were not drowned out by the booing Pats fans. Respectable showing by the Philly faithful. JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Hurts ultimately threw three interceptions in this practice, which isn’t ideal when you’re looking at the “box score.” I didn’t see all of them (there’s a lot to look at in these practices) but the one I saw was a perfectly fine short pass over the middle to Dontayvion Wicks that bounced off the receiver’s hands and into the hands of a diving Pats defender (not even fully sure that it didn’t hit the ground). The other also occurred during 7-on-7 drills, which ran concurrent with OL vs. DL 1-on-1s (which had more of my focus since they were happening right in front of me). Picks aside, let’s sort through the good and the bad. THE GOOD: Hurts’ flashiest completion was a deep ball throw to Elijah Moore, who did a nice job of tracking the ball and winning against coverage from former Eagle Kevin Byard. Moore got up and celebrated by throwing the ball … over a nearby fence (that part was unintentional, I think). Hurts threw multiple short and medium completions to Hollywood Brown, who is having his best two-day stretch of training camp. The veteran receiver proved to be a reliable target for Hurts. Hurts found a crossing Dallas Goedert in stride. Hurts hit Saquon Barkley on a screen pass where the running back was able to create an angle for lots of YAC after making the grab. I feel like I’ve noticed Hurts get better at these short passes. Hurts hit Will Shipley, who beat his defender on the wheel route, for an over-the-shoulder grab. There was a stretch where Hurts was peppering Dontayvion Wicks for short gains. Hurts found Darius Cooper along the left sideline for first down yardage. THE BAD: In addition to throwing interceptions (nine in camp so far to 10 touchdowns, though I’d argue the eye test says he’s been better than those numbers suggest), Hurts failed to lead the offense to points in the full field scrimmage towards the end of practice. (By contrast, the Pats’ starting offense moved in position for a medium-range field goal.) Hurts threw a ball behind Goedert that got knocked down. Another target to Saquon Barkley on a slant over the middle was batted down. Lettin' it fly pic.twitter.com/39Cnqb3xyL — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) August 19, 2026 While the Eagles’ passing game didn’t produce consistent results, the Pats did struggle against Philly’s ground game. Saquon Barkley seemed to have a good deal of success, as far as I could judge from a practice where tackling isn’t allowed. The Eagles’ offensive line was regularly giving him room to run. “We will see the Saquon of 2 years ago” Lane Johnson on Saquon Barkley and the running game this year. He says they are going to stretch the defense out, sideline to sideline, Lane loves what they’re doing in the running game and the screen game pic.twitter.com/tmuPOSfqeI — John Clark (@JClarkNBCS) August 19, 2026 Practice began with 1-on-1s and the first rep was a marquee matchup between A.J. Brown and Quinyon Mitchell (see videos below). As you cans see, Brown blazed past Q and was in position for the deep touchdown catch … which he failed to make. After practice, Brown “joked” that Mitchell held him, and the photo header for this article does show the brief moment of Mitchell grabbing Brown’s pants. But the refs at practice didn’t throw a flag, so, Mitchell ultimately got the stop. It was funny to hear Pats fans initially excited for what they thought was a catch, only for them to be disappointed. Eagles fans in attendance then loudly cheered the incompletion. A.J. title: A.J. Brown didn’t speak with Jalen Hurts or DeVonta Smith during Eagles-Patriots practice
summary: There were (predictably) no fireworks from the Eagles-Patriots joint practice on Wednesday, and A.J. Brown for the most part stayed clear of his former team. The WR took the practice field with a short Big Dom interaction, and then ignored nearly everyone else wearing Eagles gear as he jogged over to stretch with the Patriots. […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 19: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots drops a pass as he is defended by Quinyon Mitchell #27 of the Philadelphia Eagles during a joint practice at Gillette Stadium on August 19, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) | Getty Images There were (predictably) no fireworks from the Eagles-Patriots joint practice on Wednesday, and A.J. Brown for the most part stayed clear of his former team. The WR took the practice field with a short Big Dom interaction, and then ignored nearly everyone else wearing Eagles gear as he jogged over to stretch with the Patriots. Some may argue he was just focused on business, but another Philly alumni, Milton Williams, took a couple minutes to chop it up with head coach Nick Sirianni and a few guys from the defensive line before practice got underway. A.J. Brown jogs past former Eagles teammates on the way out to practice. pic.twitter.com/Ibb4p9Joz7 — Jimmy Kempski (@JimmyKempski) August 19, 2026 It seemed like Brown mostly — but not entirely — abstained from pleasantries during the day, and both he and his former close friends had succinct revelations about their lack of relationship. When Brown was asked if he spoke to QB Jalen Hurts since being traded, the WR simply said, “No.” He did get a follow-up question about the situation, but acknowledged that any answer to that is going to turn negative, and the WR didn’t want to feed into that. As for whether he plans to talk to Hurts when the Eagles are in New England, Brown said “sure” if they happen to cross paths — good money says they probably won’t. When DeVonta Smith was asked if he and Brown spoke during Wednesday’s practice, the Eagles WR simply said, “Nah.” There have been a lot of words from all sides about A.J. Brown’s last season in Philadelphia and his eventual trade to the Patriots, and it seems like the players, at least, are done with elaborate explanations. At this point, there’s not much else to say. There was clearly love lost over the past two seasons between teammates, and now Brown has an opportunity to start over and be the star of his story, while Hurts and Smith get a chance to prove they have everything they need to win in Philly. You’ll hear Hurts and the Eagles offense break the huddle, a protection call at the line — which seems to be a slide protection moving running back Saquon Barkley to the right — and then a throw over the middle for a touchdown to Dallas Goedert. From the eyes of QB1 pic.twitter.com/EQNisXLgJW — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) August 18, 2026 Six players we’ll be watching at Eagles-Patriots joint practices – PhillyVoice 1) QB Jalen Hurts: We’ve seen Hurts battle it out against Vic Fangio and the Eagles’ stellar defense all summer, but this will be an opportunity to run Sean Mannion’s offense against a different look, and another good defense. The Eagles’ second- and third-string units looked like crap in the first preseason game against the Ravens last Saturday. That performance was rightfully dismissed, for the most part. But certainly it will be alarming if the starters look anything like what we saw in Baltimore. Eagles-Ravens Film Review: Thoughts on Eli Stowers, Markel Bell, Willie Lampkin, and much more – BGN We are back! Sort of. The Eagles’ preseason opener was hardly an inspiring return to watching the Eagles. I am not interested in using a preseason game featuring almost no established starters to make sweeping declarations about Sean Mannion. The Eagles have repeatedly demonstrated that they are happy to sacrifice preseason entertainment to protect important players and conceal the more meaningful parts of the playbook. Whether you agree with that approach or not, this organization does not treat these games as rehearsals for its actual offense. There were still some early indications of Mannion’s influence, particularly in the running game. As part of the run-game data we are tracking for our Patreon this season, I charted six Outside Zone runs and three Duo runs. That is not a large enough sample to declare that the Eagles have transformed their offensive identity, but the emphasis was noticeable. The structure of the running game was more interesting than the results, especially when you add in more under center runs. The other important piece of context is that Baltimore’s defense was not nearly as vanilla as the Eagles’ offense. Jesse Minter called several creative pressures and tested the communication and protection rules of an inexperienced offensive line. By comparison, the Eagles kept everything extremely basic. Big Days Coming Up – Iggles Blitz These will be important days for the starters and other key players. It would be great for the Eagles to come out like a well-oiled machine and show how good they are. There will be value no matter what happens. The Eagles will find out where they stand when facing talented competition. That will tell the players and coaches what this team’s strengths and weaknesses are. A lot of attention will be on Jalen Hurts and the Eagles offense. How will they do against another team? They have gotten better during the summer so the timing of this test is good for them. Hopefully DeVonta Smith will be able to participate. He would be a difference-maker for the offense. Without him there will be a lot of pressure for the other receivers to step up. The Eagles need to get a better feel for where this WR corps is right now. Darius Cooper could use a good showing after being up and down vs the Ravens. Both Tanner McKee and Andy Dalton need a good showing after their struggles in Baltimore. The quick turnaround is probably the best thing for them. Eagles Diehard Q&A: Is the training camp vibe different for the Birds in a post-A.J. Brown world? – PHLY From Jonathan on Twitter: What’s your level of concern with Makai Lemon injury and his impact on the season since he currently isn’t practicing? Lemon seems like he’s closing in on a return after taking a big step forward in his rehab process during Monday’s practice, but he’s missed significant enough time to wonder if he’ll hit the ground running by Week 1. His role is so scheme-specific (heavy motion out of the slot, option routes, finding soft spots against specific zone coverages), it’s easy to see him needing time to master all the details. Maybe he will be comparable to Cooper DeJean in that it takes him a few weeks to break into the starting lineup at this point. Roob’s Observations: The challenge Howie Roseman faces deciding what WRs to keep – NBCSP ROSTER CONFUSION AT WIDE RECEIVER: Howie Roseman will have some interesting decisions to make on roster cutdown day Aug. 30, none more interesting than wide receiver. DeVonta Smith, Makai Lemon and Dontyvion Wicks are locks, which leaves a likely two spots for Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore, Johnny Wilson and Britain Covey to fight over. Here’s the thing. Moore and Cooper have both out-played Brown by a wide margin, but the Eagles gave Brown $5 million in guaranteed money where Moore and Cooper are on minimum-wage deals with no guarantees. Cooper has had an outstanding camp and I feel like he’s close to a lock, but Moore and Brown are both proven veterans – Brown’s had a 1,000-yard season and a couple 700-yard seasons and had 587 yards and five TDs with the Chiefs last year, and Moore averaged 50 catches for 541 yards from 2021 through 2024 with the Jets and Browns. Cooper, for all his potential, has nine career catches. Moore is more likely to clear waivers than Cooper, so the move might be to keep Brown and Cooper, cut Moore and try to get him back on the practice squad. Unless Howie decides to protect the whole group and keep six. With Lemon sidelined the last two weeks, Cooper and Moore in particular have had strong camps and both deserve to be on the roster. Wilson has a unique skill set with his physicality and blocking ability, and Covey is the Eagles’ best punt returner, but there just isn’t room for those guys. Too many wide receivers is an unusual problem for a franchise that over the past three decades years usually hasn’t had enough. Jason Kelce will call an Eagles game as ESPN expands role – Inquirer Jason Kelce spent 13 seasons with the Eagles. Now he’ll get the chance to call a Birds game. The former offensive lineman turned podcaster and ESPN announcer is jumping to the booth to call a handful of NFL games this season on the NFL Network, the network announced. Kelce will join play-by-play announcer Dave Pasch and Hall of Famer Kurt Warner to call four games, including the Eagles’ Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Oct. 11. Here are the four games Kelce, Pasch, and Warner will call: Week 4: Colts at Commanders in London (Oct. 4) … Week 5: Eagles at Jaguars in London (Oct. 11) … Week 7: Steelers at Saints in Paris (Oct. 25) … Week 16: TBD matchup (Dec. 26). title: Mason Rudolph admits jealousy towards Drew Allar, Will Howard
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers seem to be getting closer to solidifying their quarterback room. After terrific outings for all three of Mason Rudolph, Will Howard, and Drew Allar in Week 1 of the preseason, Mike McCarthy has “seen all he needs to see” from Rudolph and is giving him the week off in Week 2, meaning […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Mason Rudolph #2 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in action during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers seem to be getting closer to solidifying their quarterback room. After terrific outings for all three of Mason Rudolph, Will Howard, and Drew Allar in Week 1 of the preseason, Mike McCarthy has “seen all he needs to see” from Rudolph and is giving him the week off in Week 2, meaning it will be Howard and Allar as the only two quarterbacks when Pittsburgh hosts the New York Jets on Friday. This has led many to conclude that Rudolph’s spot on the roster is all but guaranteed, as McCarthy went out of his way to praise the veteran backup during training camp and Rudolph proceeded to go 10-of-11 in the preseason opener. Speaking to the media on Wednesday, Rudolph was very candid about knowing what the fans want – a franchise quarterback – but also being a bit envious of the advantages they have that he lacked earlier in his career. “I’m very aware that the fanbase is starved for a franchise QB,” Rudolph said, via Tim Benz . “People want to have hope for the future beyond this year. We’ve got two great QBs who are young and progressing. I really am jealous of the structure they have had and this program and this QB-grooming system the way that Coach McCarthy has done it because I feel that they have made a lot of strides. I’ll be rooting them on Friday.” It certainly didn’t go unnoticed that Rudolph took a small jab at the lack structure, one could say, in complimenting McCarthy and what he has brought to the quarterback room. It’s no secret that the Steelers struggled at the quarterback position in the post-Ben Roethlisberger world – something Rudolph was there to see first hand. From 2022-23, the quarterback room consisted of Mitch Trubisky, Rudolph, and first-round pick Kenny Pickett with Matt Canada calling plays – a far cry from a Super Bowl-winning head coach running the ship offensively. The 2023 season saw Pickett start with Trubisky and Rudolph serving as backups, with Rudolph notably swooping in for the final three games of the season to lead Pittsburgh to the playoffs, effectively ending the short-lived Pickett era. Rudolph then signed a one-year deal with the Tennessee Titans before returning to Pittsburgh in 2025 to a much warmer reception than the one he had received for the vast majority of his career. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Training camp is now in the rearview mirror, and we did not see either of the Pittsburgh Steelers’ top two defensive backs practice at all at Saint Vincent College due to injuries. Both Joey Porter Jr. and Jalen Ramsey were placed on the physically unable to perform list on July 28th as training camp began. During his Wednesday press conference, Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said the two are making progress and did not seem to have much long-term concern, per Nick Farabaugh of PennLive. Mike McCarthy says Jalen Ramsey and Joey Porter Jr. continue to make progress in their return from the PUP. Didn't see to be much long-term concern with either. — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) August 19, 2026 Ramsey suffered a knee injury during offseason minicamp. The injury did not require surgery but did keep Ramsey out for the entirety of camp. Things are a little bit more complicated with Porter Jr., who was a surprise addition to the PUP list before camp began with a back injury. However, there is plenty of reasonable speculation as to whether Porter Jr. not practicing has anything to do with his ongoing contract negotiations with the team. Seattle Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon became the highest-paid corner in NFL history with a $132 million, earning him $33 million per season. If the Steelers are to get something done with Porter Jr. before the season, we can reasonably expect the number to be at least $30 million per season. For now, it seems like McCarthy is confident that his starting defensive backs will both be healthy enough to play in the season opener against the Atlanta Falcons. The Steelers head coach emphasized the importance of letting the young guys play in the preseason, and plenty of young corners will get increased work, as they have all summer long with the absence of two of Pittsburgh’s best. full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 17: Trevon Diggs #7 of the Dallas Cowboys intercepts a pass and returns it for a 42-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on October 17, 2021 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Seattle Seahawks are in limbo as far as when they’ll sign Terrion Arnold , they have turned their attention to signing another former Alabama cornerback. Having tried out former All-Pro Trevon Diggs on Tuesday , the Seahawks have added the ex-Cowboys star to the roster on a one-year contract. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported his signing on Wednesday. Source: Former Cowboys two-time Pro-Bowl CB Trevon Diggs is signing a one-year deal with the Seattle Seahawks. pic.twitter.com/ddPVeh6WER — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 19, 2026 Diggs has prior familiarity with secondary coach Karl Scott from his Alabama days, as well current Seahawks defensive coordinator and former Cowboys assistant Aden Durde. The 27-year-old Diggs once led the league in interceptions back in 2021, recording a ridiculous 11 over 17 games. It’s been tough sledding for Diggs in terms of performance and his health in recent years, with an ACL tear in 2023 spiraling his career in a downward trajectory. Ongoing issues with his right knee, combined with repeated issues in coverage and question marks about his tackling, led to his unceremonious departure from Dallas at the end of the 2025 season. Green Bay added Diggs for a couple of games but let him go shortly after the Packers’ playoff collapse to the Chicago Bears. At his best, Diggs is a ball-hawk, but that’s also a half-decade ago and he’s been nowhere near that level. Despite his name and former prominence, it shouldn’t be assumed that Diggs is doing anything more than battling for a roster spot in a crowded but ultimately unproven cornerback room. The lack of practice time for injured third-round rookie Julian Neal may have also forced Seattle’s hand a bit as far as looking for more cornerback competition. The Seahawks confirmed the signing following their Wednesday practice, waiving recently signed wide receiver Julian Hicks to comply with the 90-man roster limit.

summary: Just a few days ago, TJ Harden recovered a fumble and had a couple of red zone carries for the Seattle Seahawks in their preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Just a few days ago, TJ Harden recovered a fumble and had a couple of red zone carries for the Seattle Seahawks in their preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Now, Harden’s next chapter could be playing… college football again?! Why yes, Harden, who was waived by the Seahawks on Monday, plans to enter the NCAA transfer portal even though his college career seemingly ended this past season at SMU. On3’s Pete Nakos has the scoop. NEW: Former Seahawks RB TJ Harden plans to enter the NCAA transfer portal, @PeteNakos reports. Harden played college ball at SMU and UCLA. https://t.co/buwHop8QDH https://t.co/t2I7fXSjkc pic.twitter.com/ktDKz88Sod — On3 (@On3) August 20, 2026 Now why would Harden be eligible to play college football when he’s completed four complete, redshirt-free seasons? Well, a Louisiana court ruling has opened the floodgates for many NFL players to make like Thornton Melon and go back to school. And this ruling may also affect Seahawks running back Anthony Hankerson , who just signed with the team and was part of the lawsuit against the NCAA. ESPN’s Dan Murphy and Pete Thamel have done the legwork on this story, so here’s the background on this lawsuit: The list of plaintiffs includes 16 football players, several who signed with NFL teams and participated in training camps earlier this month. Three of the players — Wright, Williams and former Oregon State running back Anthony Hankerson — are currently listed on NFL rosters for the Browns, Cardinals and Seahawks, respectively. […] The lawsuit claims the NCAA is breaching its “covenant of good faith” by not giving these players the same opportunity to play for five years in college that past players received and future players will receive. The NCAA changed its eligibility rules in June to allow athletes to play for five seasons within a five-year timespan which begins either when they enroll in college or in the academic year following their 19th birthday, whichever comes first. The new rule eliminates most of the waivers players received in the past to extend their time in college sports due to injuries or other extenuating circumstances. The previous eligibility rules allowed players to compete for four seasons during a five-year window without any specific age restriction. When they voted for the change, the Division I Board of Directors opted not to include outgoing seniors who played four seasons in their first four years in college even though they would have been eligible for a fifth season under the new rules. NCAA officials said they did not want a sudden influx of returning fifth-year players to take roster spots from incoming freshmen, many of whom had already signed on to play for their teams by the time the rule was changed. That decision prompted the current wave of lawsuits that have come through state and federal courts. In several cases, judges have granted temporary restraining orders that allow athletes to compete in the upcoming season while their case is pending. So not only is Harden on course for another year of college football, but so is Hankerson if he doesn’t get an NFL roster spot by the end of the month. Just another example of the wildness and chaos that is the current stage of college sports.

As the Niners enter their second preseason game, we ask what your biggest concern is about the team. What is your biggest concern for the 49ers heading into the second preseason game? We gave you four options in The Feed poll: We have to discuss the secondary based on the clips circulating from Tuesday’s joint practice. Yes, there were long-developing plays that were obviously sacks. Osa Odighizuwa and Romello Height clearly touched the quarterback. But that doesn’t ignore the consistent theme of Deommodore Lenoir, Ji’Ayir Brown, Marques Sigle, Jack Jones, and Ephesians Prysock trying to catch up to the Chargers wideouts, seemingly always a step behind. While Romello Height had a sack, is there any concern that the team still doesn’t have enough pass rushers? We know what Nick Bosa brings to the table. Still, Height is a rookie, and it’ll take time for him to find his footing. Mykel Williams is also likely to miss the first game, and maybe even land on the PUP list to begin the season. That leaves Keion White, Sam Okuayinonu, Ogbo Okronkwo, and a trio of the other veterans the Niners signed during camp. We’re also seeing other free agents, like Jadeveon Clowney and Von Miller, sign one-year deals. Wide receiver went from a strength to a potential question mark in a matter of weeks. Losing Ricky Pearsall was a major blow. De’Zhaun Stribling figures to play a prominent role in this offense, but again, he’s a rookie. Evans is excellent and will draw coverage in ways no wideout has under Kyle Shanahan. Will it be enough for the likes of Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, and Stribling to make life easier on Brock Purdy? The final option is the obvious option: Mounting injuries. You can’t have the luxury of a punting competition when you don’t have enough pass rushers to field a practice. The domino effect has taken its toll on the roster in August. Will the injury bug once again bite the Niners throughout the season?

summary: The San Francisco 49ers may have improved their defensive line, but Pro Football Focus doesn’t see that improvement as substantial. full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 13: Defensive Line Coach Kris Kocurek of the San Francisco 49ers on the sideline during the game against the Tennessee Titans at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. The Titans defeated the 49ers 19-13. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers may have improved their defensive line, but Pro Football Focus doesn’t see that improvement as substantial. And you can be optimistic and say “yet.” Ranking all the defensive lines of the NFL , PFF’s Gordon McGuinness ranked the 49ers at 20th. In June 2025 , the 49ers ranked 21st, so with Osa Odighizuwa among other things, that was just enough to move them up one spot. The addition of Osa Odighizuwa should boost the 49ers’ pass rush after the former Dallas Cowboy earned PFF pass-rush grades above 70.0 in each of the past three seasons. A fully healthy Nick Bosa would push this group much closer to the top 10 than the bottom 10, but he is coming off a season-ending injury and also missed multiple games in 2024. San Francisco would also benefit significantly from an immediate contribution from rookie Gracen Halton or a second-year leap from Alfred Collins. It should be no surprise the 49ers’ NFC West rivals, the Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks, sit in the top 10 at first and fifth, respectively. For the curious, the Arizona Cardinals, the other NFC West Rival, who ranked 20th last year, dropped all the way to 31. While the ranking is mindful of Nick Bosa’s recovery from a knee injury, it still seems like the 49ers could be slightly better than 20. That’s a big “if,” considering they need Mykel Williams back (and see if his second year isn’t stunted by his injury sustained last year), Alfred Collins needs to take a step up, and most importantly for the entire roster: be healthy through the season. At the end of the day, this line needs consistency both on the roster and on play. Last year it had 20 total sacks (which is just as small as you think). Once a starter went down, things took a gigantic step backward. If the defensive line can show they are more talented than being No. 20 in the league, it may have a trickle-down effect to improving the secondary as well, since the opposing quarterback wouldn’t have time to eat their lunch in the pocket. Do you think 20 is too low a rating for this defensive line?

Now, the Buccaneers and the veteran defensive tackle can turn their attention back to football with their defensive anchor secured. title: Do the Buccaneers actually have a good defensive front?
summary: Tampa Bay’s defense has been largely disappointing in recent seasons. The poor play can be chalked up to many different factors. One of the main culprits has been the team’s inability or down right refusal to address its once dominant defensive front— The losses of Shaq Barrett and Jason Pierre-Paul sit at the head of […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - April 24: Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2026 first round pick Rueben Bain Jr. speaks to the media during the Tampa Bay Buccaneers First Round Pick Press Conference on April 24, 2026 at the AdventHealth Training Center at One Buccaneer Place in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tampa Bay’s defense has been largely disappointing in recent seasons. The poor play can be chalked up to many different factors. One of the main culprits has been the team’s inability or down right refusal to address its once dominant defensive front— The losses of Shaq Barrett and Jason Pierre-Paul sit at the head of that table, however, names like Ndamukong Suh have a seat as well. For the first time since 2021, the Buccaneers have a defensive front that feels capable of being a (positive) focal point for their team. The conversation goes beyond just the addition of Rueben Bain Jr., who by all accounts is preparing himself to make a push for defensive rookie of the year — The Bucs actually have depth. Tampa has players and then players backing up those players who, at least in theory, can be playmakers. The “star” segments of the group would obviously be the aforementioned Bain Jr., and returning starters Yaya Diaby, Calijah Kancey, and Vita Vea. Diaby has taken some heat during his time in Tampa Bay but for most of his Tampa tenure he has played without a legitimate presence opposite him and he has still consistently produced— 19 sacks over three years, with only one campaign coming in under seven sacks. On the interior, Calijah Kancey has every bit of ability to be an elite player. The issue is Kancey’s been as hurt as Taylor Swift after a break up. Not only has the former first-round pick never played a full season but his overall games played have dropped each year he’s been in the league (14, 12, 3). In those 29 career games, Kancey’s impressively netted 11.5. If Kancey’s on the field, he’s a problem for opposing quarterbacks. If… Vita Vea. Little needs to be said about Vea. He is an elite player, one of the better Buccaneers in recent history, a potential Ring of Honor member, and another first-round pick on Tampa’s front. Vea may decide to not suit up this year amidst his contract dispute and that would leave a hole the team couldn’t mask, but we’re operating under the assumption that all players under contract will play. Aside from Bain Jr., the actual momentous improvement is in the team’s depth. Recent years have featured Chris Braswell and Anthony Nelson dominating reps off the bench and each being just one injury away from being called into full-time action. In the 2026 offseason, the Buccaneers flew into some turbulence, but they did focus their efforts on their defensive front. Among the additions: Al-Quadin Muhammed— a true veteran edge-rusher— not a flashy free agent prize, just a solid NFL vet. Muhammed is coming off an 11 sack season and brings 26 career sacks to Tampa’s rotation. On the interior of the line, the Bucs also added A’shawn Robinson. Similarly to Al-Quadin Muhammed, Robinson is not a flashy new piece. He is a reliable veteran player that Todd Bowles can depend on. Through the draft, Jason Licht gave Todd Bowles the premium golden chess piece— Rueben Bain Jr., but Tampa also added DeMonte Capehart. Capehart and Robinson aren’t the only interior linemen newly sprinkled in the equation. The Buccaneers also returned Rakeem Nunez-Roches into the mix. On the perimeter, the defense also has a quasi return in David Walker. Walker had AI levels of hype last season before suffering a season-ending injury and that hype has returned this season. In 2026, rather than Walker being in a situation where he has the upside to potentially push his way into a part-time starter’s role, he will definitively be a back up coming off the bench because the talent above him on the depth chart is cannot be unseated. Honorable mention must be given to Elijah Roberts. Roberts snuck his way into action last season and while the year was a bad look for the team it wasn’t all that bad for Roberts. As a fifth-round pick, Roberts snagged himself two sacks and recovered a fumble. Looking to maintain that momentum, he kicked off his preseason against the New York Jets with a sack and two tackles. While he isn’t likely to be a repeat headliner, Elijah Roberts represents another depth player that could be featured in some highlight packages throughout season. Pessimism around the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ defense is warranted after years of poor play, however, what was once a weakness, a void even, may have shifted to an arguable strength. For perspective, players like Chris Braswell and Anthony Nelson were near starters last year and while Nelson will certainly be a Buc in 2026 (Braswell may be) and each could see the field both are a heap of injuries away from starter-level reps.

title: Titans need defensive line, not secondary, to drive defense forward
summary: Concerns are being raised about the Tennessee Titans‘ secondary after their preseason debut. Despite fielding their starters, the secondary got taken advantage of by the San Francisco 49ers’ second-string offense. Backup quarterback Kurtis Rourke completed 12-of-14 passing attempts. Rookie receiver De’Zhaun Stribling routinely got the better off starting Titans corners Alontae Taylor and Cor’Dale Flott, […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - JUNE 17: Jeffery Simmons #98 of the Tennessee Titans speaks after the second day of minicamp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center on June 17, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Camden Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images Concerns are being raised about the Tennessee Titans ‘ secondary after their preseason debut. Despite fielding their starters, the secondary got taken advantage of by the San Francisco 49ers’ second-string offense. Backup quarterback Kurtis Rourke completed 12-of-14 passing attempts. Rookie receiver De’Zhaun Stribling routinely got the better off starting Titans corners Alontae Taylor and Cor’Dale Flott, who the team committed more than $100 million to in free agency. It’s also true that Cam Ward and the Titans’ offense have routinely gotten the better of the secondary at training camp practices. Yet the first-string offense was not productive versus the 49ers, with Ward struggling with accuracy and timing. It added another layer to the secondary discussion. Though the Titans clearly need the secondary to be more productive than they were versus the 49ers (small sample size), head coach Robert Saleh needs his defensive line to be the catalyst that drives his defense forward. The Titans’ best player on defense is unquestionably defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Saleh had full autonomy when revamping the defensive line this offseason, acquiring players he’d previously coached like John Franklin-Myers, Jermaine Johnson, Jacob Martin, Solomon Thomas, and Jordan Elliott. This Titans defense will be as productive as the front seven allows them to be. Linebackers Cedric Gray, Cody Barton, James Williams, and rookie Anthony Hill Jr. have also consistently been making plays at practice and in the preseason. Together with the defensive line, they could combine to cause havoc up front for the opposition. Taylor and Flott need to be better than they’ve been. Sophomore starters Marcus Harris and Kevin Winston Jr. need to take productive steps forward for the secondary to reach their potential. All of the above remains true, but the secondary needs Saleh’s front seven to make their lives considerably easier once regular season football begins.

title: Sonny Styles vows improvement after Commanders preseason cameo
summary: Rookie Washington linebacker Sonny Styles played his first game as an NFL player on Friday in a 20-7 preseason win over the Dolphins.   We’ll save the term “NFL debut” for games that count – that starts in Week 1 against Philly – but the No. 7 overall draft pick was in fact playing live […]
full_text: Rookie Washington linebacker Sonny Styles played his first game as an NFL player on Friday in a 20-7 preseason win over the Dolphins . We’ll save the term “NFL debut” for games that count – that starts in Week 1 against Philly – but the No. 7 overall draft pick was in fact playing live football in a Commanders uniform. For a little while, anyway. Styles played 14 defensive snaps in that contest, all of them on a 93-yard touchdown drive by the Dolphins. He sat down after that to preserve health, with a quick cameo to build on moving through training camp and the remaining preseason slate. Looking back at the performance during a Wednesday press conference, Styles “wasn’t big a fan of it.” “It was your first game and your first drive and you start slow,” he said. “There will always be things you want to be better at. … But it’s the first game. You’ve got to keep getting better.” Sonny Styles Every Snap From His NFL Debut pic.twitter.com/Na247BDJb1 — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) August 15, 2026 “If you asked him, he didn’t get downhill enough, didn’t take a shot when it was there,” head coach Dan Quinn said earlier this week. “… But, for the first time out, (he had) real command, and (was) ready to play.” Styles didn’t have a chance to find a rhythm in that game, but he has developed one in training camp practices and looked good doing it. The more opportunity Styles gets, the better he’ll be. He didn’t feel anything was different during that in-game cameo. He just needs to be himself.” “You’re a linebacker, you need to have good footwork, good hands, get off blocks and get to the ball,” Styles told on-site reporters in a Wednesday press conference . “From the game, I thought I had to clean up my footwork a little bit and to make sure I’m getting off blocks. Linemen are going to get their hands on you, and you have to use your length, but that’s the same thing (as always). Ball is ball.” Styles plays ball well. So does veteran Frankie Luvu, who looks rejuvenated in camp and has been a leader within a relatively young linebackers group. While Leo Chenal’s also in the mix at off-the-ball linebacker, it could well be Styles and Luvu partnering up regularly. Styles appreciates his presence, and the benefits of on-field work with someone like Luvu. “I’m trying to soak in as much information as I can,” Styles said. “He has been playing at a high level for a long time. I respect him a lot. It’s great to have a vet like that in the room. We’re learning how to play alongside each other. When you’re two linebackers playing next to each other a lot, you’ve got to get a feel for each other, like how each of you fit certain runs and knowing how to play off each other.” The Commanders are deep into training camp now, with 13 practices under their belts. We’re still a solid distance from regular-season action starting on Sept. 13, but improvement has been made executing coordinator Daronte Jones’ new defensive scheme. There’s a lot to learn about an attacking system that prizes versatility and moving parts, but Styles believes significant progress has been made. “We’re pretty good at knowing what to do and how to do it,” Syles said. “Now it’s about knowing why. Why are we calling this? What are we trying to defend? If we’re in this defense, what is the offense going to try and attack? That’s something Coach (Daronte Jones) talks about a lot, helping your IQ and to keep getting better in that sense.” While the Commanders defense has dealt with injuries throughout the defense, there’s a belief among the defensive players that this group will be difficult to deal with. “It’s going to be a high-level defense,” Styles said. “We’re going to help the team win. By any means necessary. We’re going to run fast, play violent and get after the ball.” How did you evaluate Sonny Styles’ performance from Friday night? Let us know in the comments below:

title: Johnny Newton Faces a Critical Crossroads in Year 3
summary: Dan Quinn’s announcement that Johnny Newton is dealing with a pectoral injury immediately raised questions about how much time the third-year defensive tackle could miss. But the bigger question for Newton now may be what happens when he returns. After two seasons that have fallen short of expectations, Newton was already entering a pivotal year […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Jer'zhan Newton #95 of the Washington Commanders looks on from the sideline during the second half of a preseason game Miami Dolphins at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dan Quinn’s announcement that Johnny Newton is dealing with a pectoral injury immediately raised questions about how much time the third-year defensive tackle could miss. But the bigger question for Newton now may be what happens when he returns. After two seasons that have fallen short of expectations, Newton was already entering a pivotal year in Washington. Now, with an injury potentially threatening his availability and his place in a crowded defensive line rotation, Newton’s window to change the trajectory of his career is beginning to close. Adam Peters selected Newton because Washington believed he had the potential to become a disruptive interior presence alongside Jonathan Allen and Daron Payne, not to simply become just a guy in a rotational role. He has not been nearly as impactful as many expected after being drafted early in the second round. Newton lost a few matchups against the run game versus the Dolphins, and it wasn’t just losing reps; that happens. It was how Newton lost them. Newton struggled to take on blocks while also giving up ground and to disengage from blockers. It contributed to a few Miami rushes that moved him off the line of scrimmage, enabling running backs to easily reach the second level. But with Newton facing a new injury and a currently unknown diagnosis, how much time exactly does Newton have to change the trajectory of his career? The odds are currently stacked against him on the roster. While he is unquestionably within the defensive line rotation, it’s easy to expect Washington to value Daron Payne, Tim Settle, Charles Omenihu, and Javon Kinlaw to have higher snap counts than Newton to start the season. Washington has options currently and doesn’t need to force him on the field if the four linemen mentioned are playing at a high level (and injury-free). If Newton cannot find a sustainable technique to stalemate anchors or generally know how to defeat blocks in the run game, his role will not increase. Even beyond a technical standpoint, Newton needs to develop the functional and core strength to consistently win in these instances and control his gaps. So time is absolutely of the essence for Newton to figure things out. full_text: The Commanders front seven has been hit hard by injuries recently, with head coach Dan Quinn reporting four new issues for that part of his defense. Interior defensive lineman Johnny Newton’s dealing with the most worrisome issue. He has a pectoral injury incurred during Friday’s preseason game versus Miami and is seeing a specialist in New York about how to handle it. Quinn said there’s concern that it’s a long-term issue. Dan Quinn gives injury updates on K'Lavon Chaisson(knee), Johnny Newton(pec), Odafe Oweh(calf), and Jordan Magee(shoulder). Newton is in New York to see a specialist, and it could be long-term. Questions from @john_keim pic.twitter.com/gUsavz4LIs — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 19, 2026 If the pec is torn and requires surgery, the injury involves a prolonged recovery and could be season-ending. Quinn said he would have an update for the media on Thursday. Linebacker Jordan Magee hurt his shoulder in the Dolphins game and he’ll be held out this week, but it’s nothing that should impact him for Week 1. The Commanders signed veteran linebacker Krys Barnes to help fill that void. The Commanders are currently working without their top edge rushers. K’Lavon Chaisson suffered a knee injury during last week’s joint practice against Miami and Odafe Oweh’s dealing with a calf strain, but neither issue is considered long term. The Commanders are being cautious/smart with both players, who are indispensable and vital to Washington’s defensive success. It will create chances for reserves to show what they can do. “The first lesson, with KC and Oweh out, here’s an opportunity for some others,” Quinn said in his Wednesday press conference . “The second lesson is, ‘what are you going to do with it?’ I don’t love injuries at all, I like when people recognize there’s an opportunity. What are they going to do about it?” Quinn also said that interior defensive lineman Tim Settle hit an important marker in his recovery from a calf strain and could be back to practice as early as Wednesday. The Commanders have a ramp-up period to help ensure a proper return to play, which was enacted with center Nick Allegretti and tight end John Bates on Tuesday and will be with the players mentioned above.

title: Commanders News: Debate continues over Jayden Daniels playing vs Lions
summary: The Daily Slop – 19 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Commanders.com Training camp […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - JANUARY 18: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders scrambles with the ball as Brian Branch #32 of the Detroit Lions dives to apply pressure during the third quarter in the NFC Divisional Playoff at Ford Field on January 18, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 19 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Commanders.com Training camp notebook | Nick Allegretti, John Bates return to practice The Commanders’ defensive front was dealing with some injuries today, as Johnny Newton, Jordan Magee, Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson were all out of practice. Quinn did not provide an update on any of the players but will likely be asked about them on Wednesday. Brandon Coleman keeps making progress at left tackle. His quick feet and hands have come in handy during pass protection, and he had a solid rep during one-on-one drills against Joshua Josephs. Chris Paul also had a positive rep working against Charles Omenihu, adjusting to Omenihu’s strength and mirroring him with good footwork. Sam Cosmi continues to dominate the drills, stopping Daron Payne in his tracks on a bull rush. Daniels threw his first pick today, but it was more an opportunistic moment for cornerback Amik Robertson as opposed to an errant throw from the quarterback. Daniels was targeting Okonkwo on the play, but the ball bounced off the tight end’s hand and into the air. Robertson was there to make the play, earning some cheers from his defensive teammates. Daniels didn’t let the play bother him, though, and connected with Jaylin Lane on his next pass attempt. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE A to Z Sports Washington Commanders lose two veteran players for the entire year before the 2026 season even begins Veteran running back Jerome Ford and veteran wide receiver River Cracraft suffered injuries during Friday’s preseason win over the Miami Dolphins , and neither will suit up for the Commanders this fall. Dan Quinn addressed Ford’s injury Tuesday when he spoke with reporters, referring to it as a hamstring injury. That’s particularly unfortunate for Ford because hamstring injuries, while fickle, are typically not long-term or serious enough to warrant an IR designation like this one. As for Cracraft, he was about to enter his ninth season in the league. He’ll still get the accrued year since he ended up on IR. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Which Commanders have the most at stake in the rest of preseason and camp? Safety: Quan Martin and Will Harris Martin, the only remaining player from the Commanders’ 2023 draft class, showed his potential in his first two seasons, but struggled last year and was benched after the team’s loss to Miami in Madrid. His play in the preseason opener against Miami last week was a reminder of his ball-hawking ability, but the team needs consistency. Harris, who signed as a free agent last year, got off to a strong start but suffered a fractured fibula in Week 3 and missed much of the season. The arrival of Cross pushed him back on the depth chart and he’s yet to stand out so far this summer. But he’s slightly bigger than Martin and has more experience. Whether one or both make the initial 53 will be impacted by other positions; will Washington keep five safeties if it feels it needs more depth on the offensive line or elsewhere? Linebacker: Ale Kaho, Kain Medrano The arrival of first-round pick Sonny Styles put the long-term futures of Kaho, Medrano and even Jordan Magee in doubt. Magee appeared to be on track to succeed Bobby Wagner inside, but that’s no longer the case — not with the selection of Styles and the signing of Leo Chenal. Kaho recorded an interception in the preseason opener, but the best path onto the roster for both players is through special teams — and that’s only if Washington intends to keep more than four linebackers. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated The Good and Not So Good From Commanders’ 12th Training Camp Practice Allegretti and Bates both went through individual drills, getting much-needed practice time and 11-on-11 work, with Allegretti also acknowledging he remains on a pitch count for now. The biggest positive is Allegretti and quarterback Jayden Daniels being on the same field again to work together. Getting their timing down is almost as important as the two getting used to one another’s technique; Allegretti has not snapped regularly since college. Bates was able to catch a pass from Daniels during team work, marking his first reception since the early portions of camp. While neither player is fully back yet, it’s good to see Washington working them back into the offense. With Newton, Magee, Oweh, and Chaisson all missing Tuesday’s practice, things were a bit thin on the defensive front Tuesday. To make things even odder, Dan Quinn didn’t address any of the players who missed practice in his pre-practice presser, leaving that up to imagination until he has a chance to clear it up in his next meeting with the media. At the end of the day, it was great for Josephs, but not the most ideal thing for Washington, who needs their top guys to be ready for the season. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE WUSA9 Brian Mitchell backs Jaylin Lane’s Commanders roster case on special teams Commanders legend Brian Mitchell says Jaylin Lane’s return ability is enough to justify a roster spot as Washington sorts through its receiver room For franchise legend Brian Mitchell, the answer that second-year receiver Jaylin Lane provides on special teams is “way more than enough to keep him around”, even if some watching the team question the validity of that stance. “I played 14 years because of my value on special teams,” Mitchell told WUSA9, pointing out the importance the unit brings to Washington football then and now. Mitchell specifically points to Lane’s two return touchdowns last season as more than enough evidence of why the young receiver should hold one of the coveted 53 spots on the active roster. He adds that with an offense and defense expected to be improved from last year’s versions, Lane’s special teams contributions, and those of others like Tyler Owens and Percy Butler, could be even more important as they look to establish solid starting positions for each unit to launch from. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Underrated Interior DL Draws Praise The interior defensive line has several pieces looking to stick out under new coordinator Daronte Jones, but the early defensive standout from Friday’s win was defensive tackle Ricky Barber. The former UDFA from last year’s class finished with a team-high five total tackles in the win, production he registered through the first half of the game, in addition to recording the Commanders’ lone sack. Head coach Dan Quinn previously praised Shy Tuttle, who finished with three tackles and one TFL vs. Miami, as a piece that has caught his eye, but Barber’s usage as a three-tech has allowed him to “penetrate and use some of his quickness” to generate enough pressure that caught Quinn’s eye. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Commanders throw a lifeline to Tre’ McKitty to finally fulfill his pre-draft promise Of course, McKitty was a highly touted college recruit at Georgia, boasting the size and athletic attributes typically associated with productive pass-catching tight ends in the pros. Despite the lack of production with the Bulldogs, the physical profile was enough for the Los Angeles Chargers to take him at No. 97 overall in the 2021 NFL Draft. Unfortunately, things haven’t gone according to plan. McKitty couldn’t firmly establish himself in Los Angeles and was…

title: Commanders 2026 Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Power Rankings – Week 2
summary: The annual Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Award competition is now well underway following the Commanders’ 20-7 beatdown of the Miami Dolphins.  Each week of the preseason, I will be publishing my own Bris Vegas Preseason Hype! Power Rankings ©, tracking the progress of the team’s late-round draft picks and undrafted roster hopefuls in generating hype through […]
full_text: The annual Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Award competition is now well underway following the Commanders’ 20-7 beatdown of the Miami Dolphins. Each week of the preseason, I will be publishing my own Bris Vegas Preseason Hype! Power Rankings ©, tracking the progress of the team’s late-round draft picks and undrafted roster hopefuls in generating hype through their efforts to claw their way onto the roster or practice squad. Players’ rankings reflect not only the hype they have generated to date, but also their potential to generate more hype as the preseason unfolds and position battles intensify ahead of roster cuts. For the benefit of new readers to the site, Hogs Haven’s annual Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Awards were named after Redskins sixth-round pick Colt Brennan and UDFA running back Marcus Mason to celebrate the struggles and occasional triumphs of players on the roster fringe battling against the odds to roster spots and playing time. Most of these players will end up on practice squads or washing out of the league. But, every season, a few of them will manage to keep their NFL dreams alive. And, as I recently showed, every Super Bowl team features at least a few major contributors who began their NFL journeys in a similar way to the players in this article. While the focus of the Mason/Brennan award is on hype, sometimes the hype turns into reality. And those of are some of the most exciting storylines of the NFL preseason and tend to produce fan favorites like Alfred Morris and Jeremy Reaves. Following the draft and UDFA signings, I previewed this year’s Mason/Brennan contestants, ranked by hype potential: Front Runners Chasing Pack Dark Horses and Longshots The first installment of the power rankings will track how they have fared compared to their initial offseason rankings. Before we get to that, let’s review the eligibility rules. The Rules Player must have been drafted late or signed by the Redskins as an undrafted free agent. Players that have only been on other teams’ practice squads that are signed by the team are also eligible. A player that has been on the team for several years is still eligible if most of that time has been spent on the practice squad, inactive, or with very limited productivity/time The Keenan “the Barbarian” Robinson Amendment: only sixth-round draft picks or later for their first two years in the league. Now that we’ve got that out of the way, here is how the race for the Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Award is shaping up, with the first preseason game in the books. Preseason Hype! – Week 2 Power Rankings Offseason preview rankings are shown in parentheses. 1. K Drew Stevens (1), no change As I mentioned in the intro, sometimes the hype turns into reality. Drew Stevens became the first Mason/Brennan contestant to graduate and become a roster lock when the Commanders released his competitor , Jake Moody, shortly after the first preseason game. I haven’t quite figured out whether that eliminates him from the competition or not. For now, he sits atop the power rankings as a shining beacon of hope for all of the other roster hopefuls fighting their own position battles. 2. RB Robert Henry Jr (11), +9 Robert Henry has shot up the board, thanks to a sizzling 75 yd/12 att (6.3 Y/A), 1 TD breakout performance in his first preseason outing. Henry’s quick burst out of his breaks was on full display as he broke off runs of 22, 15 and 24 yards through the right side of the line and around the right end. He made even more of a splash on kick returns with one allowed return for 30 yards and a second solid effort negated by a penalty. Henry had been flying under the radar, beneath a deep and underrated running back rotation in camp, before bursting onto the scene with a standout performance against the Dolphins. The Commanders’ decision on which running backs to keep just became a lot more complicated. Sam in BrisVegas: I was on to Henry before it was cool. He’s going to be good. 3. WR Jaden “Moss” Bradley (5), +2 In hindsight, it is hard to believe that Jaden Bradley was ranked as low as fifth before the pads came on. Bradley evaded notice of the draft media, despite posting a 58 rec, 931 yd, 4 TD stat line in his fifth college season at UNLV. As foreshadowed in the Mason/Brennan Preview , Bradley has lived up to his hype potential, with a standout performance in camp raising questions about how many receivers the Commanders will keep on the 53-man roster. Bradley’s hopes of earning a roster spot seemed to take a hit, with the Stefon Diggs signing , along with all of the other roster hopefuls at receiver. But he might force a rethink if he can maintain the momentum he established in training camp. He didn’t hurt his chances with a solid outing in the first preseason game, catching 2-of-3 targets from quarterbacks Sam Hartman and Athan Kaliakmanis for 21 total yards and 11 YAC with one drop, and nearly blocking two punts. 4. QB Athan Kaliakmanis (17), +13 Athan Kaliakmanis seemed to be facing a ceiling on his preseason hype potential when I wrote the preview, because he was battling for the third string QB position. That was before an injury to primary backup Marcus Mariota in the preseason opener created an opening. Kaliakmanis seized the opportunity, with a strong debut performance, to leapfrog Sam Hartman into the next position on the depth chart. If Mariota misses significant time — the Commanders are optmistic Mariota will be ready for Week 1 — Kaliakmanis has positioned himself to be Jayden Daniels’ game day backup. 5. RB Kaytron Allen (2), -3 Kaytron Allen hasn’t done anything to hurt his hype potential. He was simply overtaken by the hype trains building behind Robert Henry and Athan Kaliakmanis. Allen has had a solid camp and delivered a strong performance in the preseason opener, leading the Commanders in rushing yards (23 att, 85 yds, 3.7 Y/A) and scoring his first NFL TD. 6. DT Ricky Barber (6), no change Ricky Barber was almost scratched from consideration, because of his off-the charts productivity (3 comb tackles, 1 TFL, 1 sack, 1 QB hit, 25% pressure rate) in 15 defensive snaps last season. But I bent the rules to keep him in it by leaning on the fact that he has had “very limited… time .” Barber flashed hype potential with a strong performance against the Dolphins. Lining up predominantly at right defensive tackle, he was a force in the A-gaps. Barber co-led the team with three defensive stops, along with fellow interior defensive lineman Shy Tuttle, and was second in pressures with one quarterback hit and one hurry. If he keeps up that pace, he might force his way onto the roster or at least reclaim his position on the practice squad. 7. C Matt Gulbin (4), -3 The Commanders’ pivot to Julian Good-Jones when starting center Nick Allegretti was injured was a setback to Gulbin’s preseason hype campaign, without a doubt. Gulbin fought back the best way he could, with a strong outing in pass protection (0 pressures allowed). He opened running lanes for Robert Henry Jr. and Kaytron Allen and did a good job climbing to the next level to seal off defenders in the preseason opener. Those fans hoping to see Gulbin battling for the starting center job might get something to cheer for if he can keep building on that performance. 8. S Malik Spencer (7), -1 Malik Spencer announced his presence by making the first interception of training camp, then followed that up with strong practice performances and another interception in the first preseason game. Spencer is a versatile defensive back who can play everything from nickel to box and free safety and even a bit of dime ‘backer. He has the advantage of competing in the thinnest position group on the roster. If he can keep drawing the coaches’ attention with big takeaways, he has a shot of beating out Percy Butler for the last safety spot. 9.
